attrs.statement: An affiliate moves through Pending (account created, password not yet set) → Active (password set, transacting) and may then be Suspended (temporary, reversible, codes disabled, pending commissions held pending investigation — B3) or Inactive (permanent terminal end-of-partnership, codes disabled, portal read-only, final balance settled/forfeited/written off — B5). Active ⇄ Suspended is reversible via Screen 3.1; Active → Inactive is terminal via Screen 3.3 and is not silently reversed (resuming requires re-onboarding).
attrs.rationale: PRD General Module Rules, prd.md line 1174

attrs.statement: A code's `Maximum Usage Count` and `Per-Patient Usage Limit` are decremented on "completed" (paid) redemptions only, never on "applied" events — so abandoned or abusive checkouts cannot exhaust a code's cap. A separate soft anti-abuse rate limit on "applied" events (per patient / per IP / per time window) guards against application spam without consuming the usage cap.
attrs.rationale: PRD General Module Rules, prd.md line 1175

attrs.statement: Percentage commissions are calculated as a percentage of the completed booking's revenue (booking total, in USD per the Currency Rule) — not as a percentage of Hairline's net commission. Fixed-amount commissions are a flat USD amount per completed booking, independent of booking value. In both cases the commission is funded from (deducted from) Hairline's commission, never the provider's payout (Rule 4). The patient-facing affiliate discount (also Hairline-funded, Rule 2) and the affiliate commission are separate Hairline-borne costs against the same booking.
attrs.rationale: PRD General Module Rules, prd.md line 1176

attrs.statement: On any single booking, the combined Hairline-funded cost — the patient-facing affiliate discount (Rule 2) plus the affiliate commission (Rule 14) — MUST NOT exceed Hairline's own commission earned on that booking; the affiliate program never makes a booking net-negative for Hairline. The system enforces this at affiliate code creation/generation (Screen 4): when both the discount and the commission are percentage-based, it validates that `discount % + commission % ≤ Hairline's commission % on the booking` and blocks the save with the shortfall shown; an admin with documented business approval may override with an audited confirmation. Fixed-amount configurations (where the ceiling depends on booking value) raise a review warning rather than a hard block, since the breach can only be evaluated per booking. This rule complements Assumption 4 (aggregate program cost ≤ 10% of Hairline commission revenue) by preventing per-booking negative margin.
attrs.rationale: PRD General Module Rules, prd.md line 1177

attrs.statement: Performance Tier (system-calculated, read-only): a band derived from the affiliate's trailing-12-month revenue generated (USD) by completed referrals, recalculated monthly. Default bands (admin-tunable): Bronze < $5,000 · Silver $5,000–$24,999 · Gold $25,000–$99,999 · Platinum ≥ $100,000. attrs.statement: Currency Rule: All affiliate amounts (commission accrual, pending balances, thresholds, and payouts) are denominated in USD — the platform base currency owned by FR-029 (Payment System Configuration). When a booking is transacted in a non-USD currency, its value is converted to USD using FR-029's currency service, supported-currency list, and locked exchange-rate/markup logic — FR-018 never defines, caches, or overrides its own FX rate. The conversion rate applied to a commission is the rate locked for that booking per FR-029 (no discrepancy with billing/finance figures). Affiliates are responsible for any onward conversion from USD on their side. Note on client figures: GBP amounts in the client transcription (e.g., "£50", "£200") are illustrative of intended incentive magnitudes; the platform base currency is USD (per FR-029), so this PRD's literal thresholds and minimums (e.g., the $50 minimum fixed commission and $50 payout threshold) are stated in USD and are not a direct GBP→USD conversion of those examples.

nodes.title: Auto-applied use: reserve at send, one per sent quote, release or consume by outcome

attrs.statement: For an auto-applied promotion, System MUST reserve one use when a quote carrying it is sent, MUST hold at most one reserved use per sent quote across re-sent versions (keeping the existing reservation, creating one only when a new version newly carries the promotion, and releasing it when a new version no longer carries the promotion), MUST release the reservation when the quote expires, is withdrawn, ends Not Selected, drops the promotion in a re-sent version, or is cancelled before acceptance because the inquiry was cancelled or the provider's status changed, or when a subquote of that quote is accepted that does not carry the promotion (`not_applied`), and MUST consume it when the accepted subquote carries the promotion. If the booking reaches `Payment Window Expired` or is cancelled before the first payment, System MUST return the consumed use to the limit; on an admin revive, System MUST take the use again if the limit has room and otherwise MUST reject the revive, so the accepted price never changes. Usage limits MUST count active reservations plus consumed uses so that a limit can never be exceeded.
attrs.rationale: Restated by Scope Boundaries, Alternative Flows A3 and A5, Screen 6 rules and General Module Rules. PRD lines 58, 144-145, 157, 727, 729.

attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B1. PRD lines 118-120. Screen 11 business rules (line 681) add segment-mismatched codes to the list of reasons shown.

nodes.title: A second discount entered by the user prompts a replace-or-keep choice

attrs.statement: Trigger: Before the quote is sent (provider) or before the subquote is accepted (patient), the user manually enters or selects a second discount for an option/date-price row (subquote) that already has one. Steps: System blocks the new entry; prompts the user to confirm replacement or keep the existing discount. A patient's replacement applies only to the patient's selection on that subquote and never changes the provider's promotion. Outcome: Exactly one discount per subquote; the user's confirmed choice is applied. After acceptance no entry, selection, or replacement is accepted (Alternative Flow B4).
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B2. PRD lines 124-126. Screen 11 business rule (line 677) and acceptance criterion 2 (line 688: audit records both events) repeat it for the patient.

nodes.title: Auto-applied conflicts resolve silently by priority, with no user prompt

attrs.statement: Trigger: When a quote is sent, more than one automatic promotion is eligible for the quote, or an automatic promotion is eligible for an option/date-price row that already carries another discount. Steps: A quote carries at most one automatic promotion. System silently resolves the conflict using the priority order: patient-entered code > provider discount (provider-selected or provider auto-applied) > Hairline-funded discount > affiliate discount. When several automatic programs qualify, only the highest-ranked one attaches, to every row it is eligible for; the others attach to no row of that quote and reserve no use. On a row that already carries a higher-ranked discount, the automatic promotion is not applied to that row. No user prompt is shown. Example: A Hairline-funded automatic program and a provider's automatic program are both eligible when a quote is sent. The provider's program ranks higher, so it attaches to every row it is eligible for and one use is reserved for it; the Hairline-funded program attaches to no row of that quote and no use is reserved for it.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B3. PRD lines 130-132. General Module Rules (line 721) repeat the priority order.

nodes.title: Exactly one discount affects the price; audit records applied and superseded programs; affiliate attribution is preserved

attrs.statement: Outcome: Exactly one discount affects the patient's final price; audit records which program was applied and which was superseded. If a valid affiliate-bound code/link was already captured as the patient acquisition source, FR-019 preserves that affiliate attribution metadata for FR-018 even when a provider-side promotion wins the price-discount priority.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B3 outcome. PRD line 133.

nodes.title: Direct-issued code is validated against its binding and redemption is recorded against the issuing channel

attrs.statement: Trigger: Admin issues a Hairline-funded code (open code, segment-bound, or affiliate-distributed) and the patient enters it on one named subquote before acceptance. Steps: System validates the code against issuance binding (open vs recipient-bound), records the redemption against the issuing channel (e.g., affiliate id), and calculates commission on the accepted price after the promotion, as for every discount type. For affiliate-bound codes, code generation and affiliate assignment are initiated from FR-018; FR-019 receives the registered code and manages redemption lifecycle. Outcome: Patient receives discount; the platform commission and the provider's payout are both reduced, with the provider bearing most of the discount; affiliate (if applicable) accrues the configured incentive (see FR-018).
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow C1. PRD lines 137-139.

nodes.title: Automatic promotion attaches at send to every eligible row; the provider price stays and the discount shows as a separate line

attrs.statement: Trigger: A provider sends a quote while an auto-applied program is active and eligible for one or more of its option/date-price rows. Steps: A quote carries at most one automatic promotion; when several qualify, Alternative Flow B3 picks one. System attaches that program to every eligible option/date-price row of the sent quote and copies its terms into the sent quote version. The provider's entered price on each row stays unchanged, and the discount is shown as a separate line next to it. Rows that are not eligible receive no automatic promotion. Conflicts with another discount on the same row are resolved by Alternative Flow B3. Sending a quote carrying the automatic promotion reserves one use against the program's usage limits. A sent quote holds at most one reserved use: re-sending a new version keeps the existing reservation, creates one only if the new version newly carries the promotion, and releases it if the new version no longer carries the promotion. If the limit is already fully reserved or consumed, the promotion does not attach.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A3. PRD lines 143-146, General Module Rules (line 724). Outcome and exception lines are carried by REQ-019-012, REQ-019-015 and REQ-019-019.

nodes.title: Patient code is validated for the named subquote only and never written to the provider promotion

attrs.statement: Trigger: While reviewing one named subquote and before confirming acceptance, the patient enters a code (FR-005 Alternative Flow A8). Steps: System validates the code for that subquote only (active window, eligibility, usage limits, recipient binding). If valid, the discounted price is shown next to the provider's offered price; if invalid, the reason is shown and the offered price is unchanged. The code is recorded against the patient's selection on that subquote and is never written to the provider's promotion or quote records. Opening another subquote does not carry the code over. Outcome: On acceptance, the discounted price and the applied promotion are frozen into the AcceptanceEvent snapshot.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A4. PRD lines 150-152. Screen 11 business rule (line 678) and acceptance criterion 3 (line 688) repeat that the code is not carried to another subquote.

nodes.title: Accepting a subquote with a promotion creates one Application atomically and reserves or consumes a use

attrs.statement: Trigger: The patient accepts a subquote that carries a promotion attached at send or a valid patient-entered code. Steps: In the same atomic step as the acceptance, the system creates one Application linked to the AcceptanceEvent, the parent quote and version, and the accepted option/date-price row, and reserves one use against the program's usage limits. For an automatic promotion attached at send, the use already reserved at send is consumed instead. If the accepted subquote does not carry the automatic promotion that reserved a use for its parent quote, that reservation is released with reason `not_applied` and the use returns to the limit. Sibling subquotes marked Not Selected and competing quotes never create an Application; any use reserved for them at send is released. A patient code entered on a subquote that was not accepted is discarded. Outcome: The Application is in state Applied with its use reserved, or consumed for an automatic promotion; the discounted price is read from the acceptance snapshot by every later step.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A5. PRD lines 156-158, Implementation Notes (line 814).

nodes.title: Any promotion change attempted after acceptance is rejected and logged

attrs.statement: Trigger: Any actor (patient, provider, or admin) tries to remove, replace, enter, or revalidate a promotion on an accepted subquote, including at checkout or booking. Steps: System rejects the action, leaves the Application and the AcceptanceEvent snapshot unchanged, and logs the attempt. Outcome: The accepted price stands. The only exception is the provider-fault transfer in FR-006 (Alternative Flow B5), which creates a new linked acceptance record; promotion handling for that case follows the post-acceptance freeze rule in General Module Rules.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B4. PRD lines 162-164. Screen 11 business rule (line 680) and Screen 11 acceptance criterion 4 (line 689) repeat the rejection at checkout and payment.

nodes.title: Three program types share one governance model

attrs.statement: This module exposes **three promotion programs** under one unified governance model: **Admin-via-Provider** — Admin defines a campaign that affects both Hairline and provider fees; targeted providers must opt-in before the code becomes selectable on their quotes. **Provider Self-Created** — Provider defines a discount on their own quotes; no admin approval required. **Hairline-Funded & Direct-Issued** — Admin defines a Hairline-only discount that is issued directly to patients (open-entry code, patient-segment-bound, affiliate-distributed, or individually issued); providers are not involved in approval.
attrs.rationale: Screen Specifications overview. PRD lines 170-176.

nodes.title: Admin may pause or revoke adoption on any program and record a refund; no actor may change the promotion on an accepted subquote

attrs.statement: All three program types share a single `PromotionProgram` entity (see Key Entities) and are managed through a unified screen system with type-aware filters, forms, and analytics. Admin retains override authority on every program (pause, revoke adoption) and may record a refund through FR-017 regardless of program type. No actor, including admin, may void, remove, or change the promotion on an accepted subquote (Alternative Flow B4).
attrs.rationale: Screen Specifications overview. PRD line 178.

nodes.title: The hub lists every program type in one catalog with a default sort and result count; filters combine as AND

attrs.statement: All three program types appear in this hub; the Program Type filter narrows the view. Given the admin opens the Hub, when the screen loads, then the system shows all program types in one list with the default descending Last Updated sort and the result count for the default query. Given the admin applies any combination of Program Type, Status, Funding Model, Provider Participation, Date Range, Usage, and ROI filters, then the catalog returns only rows satisfying all active filters and updates the result count. Given the admin selects a row, then the system opens Screen 2 for that program without losing catalog context.
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 (Promotion Program Hub) business rules and acceptance criteria 1-3. PRD lines 245, 252-254.

nodes.title: Admin monitors provider self-created programs and may pause or archive them; editing stays with the provider

attrs.statement: Provider Self-Created programs appear here so admins can monitor and intervene; admins may pause or archive any program but typically do not edit provider-owned definitions (see Screen 4 Notes). Admin may open Screen 2 in read-only mode for provider self-created programs; editing is reserved for the provider unless an override is needed (governance action, logged in audit). Admin may pause or archive any provider self-created program via row action with mandatory reason text.
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 business rules and Screen 4 business rules. PRD lines 246, 397-398. Screen 4 notes (lines 400-402) record that this goes beyond the client transcription.

nodes.title: Hub search, filter, result count and reset behaviour stay aligned with FR-022

attrs.statement: Search, filter, result count, and reset behavior must stay aligned with FR-022 control standards. Search and filter field definitions are co-owned with FR-022. Any change must be updated in both FR-019 and FR-022.
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 business rules and notes. PRD lines 247, 259. FR-022 co-owns the field definitions.

nodes.title: Pausing a program keeps redemptions intact and stops new attachment and code validation

attrs.statement: Given the admin triggers Pause on an Active program row, then the program lifecycle transitions to Paused, all existing redemptions remain intact, the program is not attached to newly sent quotes and does not validate new patient codes, and option/date-price rows already sent keep the terms copied at send.
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 acceptance criterion 4. PRD line 255. Sent rows keep the terms copied at send (REQ-019-012).

nodes.title: Program form limits: name and description length, end not before start, usage limits non-negative

attrs.statement: Program Name: 3–120 chars. Description: ≤ 1000 chars. Start / End Date: End ≥ Start. Total Usage Limit: ≥ 0; blank = unlimited. Per-User Usage Limit: ≥ 0; blank = unlimited.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 common data fields, validation column, composed from table cells. PRD lines 271-280. Screen 9 rows 585-593 repeat the same limits.

nodes.title: Program lifecycle state moves forward only

attrs.statement: Lifecycle State: Draft → Active → Paused → Expired → Archived; Forward transitions only.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 common data fields, composed from the table row. PRD line 281. Row actions Pause and Resume on Screens 1 and 8 and the Pending Approval state on Screen 1 do not fit a forward-only sequence (open item).

nodes.title: Funding model is derived from the program type and cannot be set independently

attrs.statement: `Funding Model` is derived from `Program Type` and cannot be set independently.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 business rules. PRD lines 302, 287, 381, 601 (Provider Only is fixed on the provider form).

nodes.title: Saving an Admin-via-Provider program sets Pending Approval and notifies targeted providers

attrs.statement: For Admin-via-Provider, saving transitions the program to `Pending Approval` and notifies targeted providers (S-03).
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 business rules. PRD line 303; same outcome as the Main Flow step 2 rule.

nodes.title: Auto-applied mode is allowed only for Hairline Only or Provider Only programs and never on a replacement quote

attrs.statement: `Application Mode = Auto-applied` is only allowed for programs with `Funding Model = Hairline Only` or `Provider Only` and explicit eligibility rules (cannot be auto-applied across multiple providers without consent). Auto-applied programs attach when a quote is sent (Alternative Flow A3). They never attach to an admin-authored replacement quote, and no use is reserved for one.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 business rules. PRD line 305, acceptance criterion 4 (line 315: message "Auto-applied is not permitted for Both-Fees programs.").

nodes.title: Hairline share percent is required for Both Fees programs, 0 to 100, audited, and part of the terms fixed at send

attrs.statement: `Hairline Share %` is required for Both Fees programs and must be a number from 0 to 100; it is hidden for other funding models. It is part of the terms fixed at send and frozen at acceptance, so an edit applies only to quotes sent afterwards. Every change is recorded in the Audit Trail Panel with actor, timestamp, and old and new values.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 business rules. PRD line 306, acceptance criterion 5 (line 316).

nodes.title: Bulk upload and bulk edit are available for campaign management

attrs.statement: Bulk upload / bulk edit available for campaign management.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 business rules. PRD line 308.

nodes.title: A single open code is redeemable by any patient as soon as the program is published

attrs.statement: Given the admin creates a Hairline-Funded program with `Issuance Channel = Open code` and a single code, when the program is published, then the code is immediately redeemable by any patient on a named subquote before acceptance and the program does not appear in any provider's adoption inbox.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 acceptance criterion 2. PRD line 313.

nodes.title: Application mode options differ by program type by design

attrs.statement: `Application Mode` options differ by Program Type by design: admin programs use `Auto-applied / Code-only` (no list-selection because admin programs are not shown in a provider's quote-creation picker — they are adopted via the approval workflow and then selected from the provider's adopted campaigns list); provider programs use `List-selection / Code-only / Either`.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 notes. PRD line 321. Conflicts with Screen 9 and FR-004 on how admin programs reach a quote (open item).

nodes.title: All state changes, edits, approvals and overrides are listed in time order with actor, time and reason

attrs.statement: All state changes, edits, approvals, and override actions are listed in chronological order with actor, timestamp, and reason.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 audit trail panel. PRD line 298.

nodes.title: Bulk code generation creates N unique codes, quantity 1 to 10,000

attrs.statement: Bulk Generate Codes: Generate N unique codes for distribution; quantity 1–10,000
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 type-specific fields, composed from the table row. PRD line 294.

nodes.title: Force-Revoke removes the program from the provider's selection list at once and keeps in-flight quotes

attrs.statement: Force-Revoke immediately removes the program from the provider's quote-creation selection list; in-flight quotes with the program already applied are preserved.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 business rules. PRD line 350, acceptance criterion 1 (line 356: within 5 seconds).

nodes.title: Re-invite resets a declined or auto-declined provider to Pending and re-sends the notification

attrs.statement: Re-invite resets the provider's status from Declined or Auto-Declined back to Pending and re-sends the S-03 notification.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 business rules. PRD line 351.

nodes.title: Every admin override requires reason text in the audit trail

attrs.statement: All admin overrides are logged with mandatory reason text in the audit trail.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 business rules. PRD line 352.

nodes.title: An approval request with no response auto-declines after the window and is visible in audit

attrs.statement: Given the program's Auto-Decline Window elapses without a provider decision, then the provider's status updates to Auto-Declined and is visible in this manager. Auto-Decline triggers if the Auto-Decline Window (Screen 2) elapses without a decision.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 acceptance criterion 2, Screen 7 business rules and edge cases. PRD lines 357, 535, 902.

nodes.title: An open code serves any eligible patient until the total usage limit is reached

attrs.statement: Open codes have one code that any eligible patient may use until the total usage limit is reached.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 business rules. PRD line 436.

nodes.title: Segment-bound codes validate the patient against the segment at entry time

attrs.statement: Segment-bound codes validate the patient against the segment definition at entry time.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 business rules. PRD line 438.

nodes.title: Individually-issued codes are single-use and bound to one patient

attrs.statement: Individually-issued codes are single-use and bound to a specific patient identifier.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 business rules. PRD line 439.

nodes.title: Revoking a code stops validation on unaccepted subquotes but not a reserved use

attrs.statement: Revoking a code stops it from validating on any subquote not yet accepted. A use already reserved by an accepted subquote (`In-Progress`) stays frozen with the acceptance and is not cancelled by the revoke.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 business rules. PRD line 440. Bulk Revoke needs a mandatory reason (line 418).

nodes.title: Bulk Generate for 50 selected affiliates creates 50 unique codes, one per affiliate

attrs.statement: Given the admin selects a Hairline-Funded program with channel = Affiliate-bound and triggers Bulk Generate for 50 selected affiliates, when generation completes, then 50 unique codes are created, each code is bound to exactly one affiliate, and each appears in the table with status = Unused.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 acceptance criterion 1. PRD line 444. Conflicts with the FR-018 generation boundary (open item).

nodes.title: First successful payment on an affiliate-bound code marks it Redeemed and triggers the affiliate incentive event

attrs.statement: FR-018: Affiliate Management – Affiliate-bound code redemptions accrue incentive to the linked affiliate; FR-019 triggers the incentive event consumed by FR-018. Given a patient enters an Affiliate-bound code on a named subquote and accepts it, when the first payment succeeds, then the corresponding row updates to Redeemed and the affiliate's incentive accrual (per FR-018) is triggered.
attrs.rationale: Internal Dependencies (FR-018) and Screen 5 acceptance criterion 2. PRD lines 437, 445, 775.

nodes.title: Applied and Completed are two distinct redemption states

attrs.statement: The two-state distinction (Applied vs Completed) is preserved per client request (Admin Part 1 L341–344). Applied = the subquote carrying the promotion has been accepted and, for a provider-selected promotion or patient code, one use is reserved; Completed = the first payment for that booking has succeeded and that reserved use is consumed. For an automatic promotion the use is already consumed at acceptance, so Completed only marks the first payment.
attrs.rationale: Screen 6 business rules. PRD line 492.

nodes.title: Voided and Superseded are set only by the system; there is no admin Void

attrs.statement: Voided is set only by the system, when the booking reaches `Payment Window Expired` or is cancelled; the reserved use is then released. For an automatic promotion, the use consumed at acceptance returns to the usage limit when the row is Voided before the first payment. Superseded is set only by the system when a provider-fault transfer replaces the accepted record. There is no admin Void action.
attrs.rationale: Screen 6 business rules. PRD line 493, acceptance criteria 3 and 4 (lines 501-502).

nodes.title: Reverse and Refund are logged with a reason, integrate with FR-017 and never change the accepted price

attrs.statement: Reverse / Refund actions are logged with mandatory reason and integrate with FR-017 (Billing & Finance) for monetary reconciliation. They never change the accepted price or the AcceptanceEvent snapshot.
attrs.rationale: Screen 6 business rules. PRD line 494, acceptance criterion 2 (line 500: status Refunded, FR-017 receives a reconciliation event).

nodes.title: The first successful payment moves Applied to Completed and consumes the reserved use

attrs.statement: Given an accepted subquote with an Applied redemption, when the first payment for the booking succeeds, then the redemption row transitions from State = Applied to State = Completed, the reserved use is consumed (for an automatic promotion the use was already consumed at acceptance and is not counted again), and the change is reflected in Overview KPIs within 5 seconds.
attrs.rationale: Screen 6 acceptance criterion 1. PRD line 499, Screen 6 rule on automatic promotions (line 492).

nodes.title: Revoking an adoption does not affect quotes that already have the program applied

attrs.statement: Revoking adoption does not affect quotes that already have the program applied; only new selections are blocked.
attrs.rationale: Screen 7 business rules. PRD line 534.

nodes.title: Revoking an adoption requires a reason and ends in Revoked-by-Provider

attrs.statement: Given an Active campaign, when the provider clicks Revoke Adoption with reason, then the campaign moves to Past with state = Revoked-by-Provider and is no longer offered in quote creation.
attrs.rationale: Screen 7 acceptance criterion 2. PRD line 540.

nodes.title: A provider may run many self-created promotions at once, subject to one discount per booking

attrs.statement: Provider may have an arbitrary number of self-created promotions concurrently active, subject to the platform's single-discount-per-booking rule at redemption time.
attrs.rationale: Screen 8 business rules. PRD line 566.

attrs.statement: Code uniqueness enforced platform-wide (cannot collide with admin codes or other providers' codes).
attrs.rationale: Screen 8 business rules. PRD line 567, Screen 2 field rows (lines 276, 589). Format policy is admin configurable (PRD line 745).

nodes.title: The code is optional on provider self-created promotions; the default mode is list selection

attrs.statement: The **Code field is optional** per a deliberate scope decision. The client transcription (Provider Part 2 L27–33) stated codes are not relevant for provider self-created discounts since providers select them from a list during quote creation. This FR retains the field as **optional** so providers may also issue code-based promotions for marketing distribution (e.g., flyer codes, partner promos). Default Application Mode is `List-selection during quote`.
attrs.rationale: Screen 9 business rules. PRD line 598, scope note (line 615). A scope extension beyond the client transcription (open item).

nodes.title: Ad-hoc records are scoped to one quote and hidden from other quotes' pickers

attrs.statement: **Mode 2 ad-hoc records** are scoped to a single quote and are not shown in the list-selection picker on other quotes' creation screens. They remain visible to admin in Screen 1 Hub (Scope filter = Ad-Hoc Quote-Bound) and Screen 4 Portfolio.
attrs.rationale: Screen 9 business rules. PRD line 599.

nodes.title: A promotion on a row changes only while the quote is drafted or revised before acceptance

attrs.statement: A promotion selected on an option/date-price row may be changed only while the quote is drafted or revised in FR-004 before acceptance. Its terms are copied into the sent quote version when the quote is sent, and a promotion can apply only to a row it was attached to at send.
attrs.rationale: Screen 9 business rules and Screen 10 business rules. PRD lines 603, 652.

nodes.title: A code-only promotion is hidden from the quote picker and redeemable by code on a named subquote

attrs.statement: Given the provider saves a Mode 1 promotion with a Code and Application Mode = Code-only, then the promotion is not shown in the quote-creation selection list but is redeemable when the patient enters the code on a named subquote of that provider's quote before acceptance.
attrs.rationale: Screen 9 acceptance criterion 2. PRD line 608.

nodes.title: Saving an ad-hoc promotion as reusable clears both bindings and makes it selectable on future quotes

attrs.statement: Given the provider saves a Mode 2 ad-hoc promotion with "Save as reusable" enabled, then `scope = REUSABLE` is recorded and the promotion becomes selectable on future quotes within its active window.
attrs.rationale: Screen 9 acceptance criterion 4. PRD line 610.

nodes.title: Ad-hoc promotion defaults: active window of the bound quote, total limit 1 unless saved as reusable

attrs.statement: Start / End Date: Mode 1: end ≥ start. Mode 2: defaults to the active window of the bound quote. Total Usage Limit: ≥ 0; blank = unlimited. Mode 2 forces total limit = 1 unless "Save as reusable" is toggled.
attrs.rationale: Screen 9 data fields, composed from table cells. PRD lines 591-592.

nodes.title: A provider cannot reverse a Completed redemption; that authority is admin's

attrs.statement: The provider cannot reverse a Completed redemption; that authority sits with admin (Screen 6).
attrs.rationale: Screen 10 business rules. PRD line 653.

nodes.title: A code is validated at entry and again when the patient confirms acceptance

attrs.statement: Validation occurs when the code is entered and again when the patient confirms acceptance. On acceptance, the discounted price is frozen into the AcceptanceEvent snapshot.
attrs.rationale: Screen 11 business rules. PRD line 679, edge case on a code no longer valid at confirmation.

nodes.title: A partial-scope discount shows which price line it reduces

attrs.statement: Where a discount applies only to a sub-component (e.g., treatment cost, not travel), the breakdown explicitly shows which line is reduced.
attrs.rationale: Screen 11 business rules. PRD line 682, acceptance criterion 1 (line 686: breakdown updates within 1 second with the scope label).

nodes.title: Active dates, eligibility and usage limits are checked at attach and at code validation

attrs.statement: Active dates, eligibility, and usage limits are checked when a promotion is attached to a row at send and when a patient code is validated before acceptance.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rules. PRD line 723.

nodes.title: A promotion applies only to the row it was attached to at send or the one named subquote

attrs.statement: A promotion applies only to an option/date-price row it was attached to at send, or to the one named subquote on which the patient entered a code. Any other application is rejected.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rules. PRD line 725, Screen 9 acceptance criterion 5 (line 611), User Story 4 scenario 4.

nodes.title: A fully reserved or consumed limit blocks attach at send and fails code validation

attrs.statement: Usage limits count active reservations plus consumed uses, so a limit can never be exceeded. A promotion whose limit is fully reserved or consumed does not attach at send and fails code validation.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rules. PRD line 728; the counting sentence is also in REQ-019-015.

nodes.title: On a provider-fault transfer the original Application is kept as Superseded and a new Application is linked

attrs.statement: Post-acceptance freeze: after acceptance, the promotion and discounted price of the accepted subquote are frozen in the AcceptanceEvent snapshot. No removal, replacement, code entry at checkout or booking, price-changing revalidation, or admin void is allowed. The only exception is the provider-fault transfer in FR-006 (Alternative Flow B5): the original Application is kept as history and marked Superseded, and any promotion on the replacement is recorded as a new Application linked to the new admin-authored acceptance record; a use already reserved or consumed carries over and is not counted twice. Money handling for that transfer is defined by FR-006, FR-007, FR-007b, and FR-017.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rules, post-acceptance freeze exception. PRD line 730. FR-006 Alternative Flow B5 owns the transfer.

nodes.title: All discount creations, approvals, applications and removals are auditable

attrs.statement: All discount creations, approvals, applications, and removals are auditable.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rules. PRD line 733.

nodes.title: Patients see only non-sensitive discount information; cost splits stay internal

attrs.statement: Display only non‑sensitive discount info to patients; provider/Hairline cost splits remain internal.

nodes.title: Financial records and discount artifacts are kept at least 7 years; takedown is by archival

nodes.title: Admin edits discount categories, code format policy, max value caps, dates, targeting, approval routing and templates

attrs.statement: Discount categories, code format policy, max value caps, and campaign dates. Targeting rules (all providers vs. subsets) and approval routing. Notification templates for approvals and status.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules. PRD lines 745-747.

nodes.title: Max discount value per policy and region and the auto-decline window are configurable with restrictions

attrs.statement: Max discount value thresholds per policy and region. Auto‑decline window for unresponded provider approvals.

nodes.title: Single-discount rule, priority order, terms fixed at send and calculation order are fixed in code

attrs.statement: Single‑discount rule and priority order. Promotion terms fixed at send and frozen at acceptance. Calculation order of operations (base → discounts → taxes/fees).

nodes.title: The Application and the usage reservation are created atomically with acceptance; payment never recomputes the price

attrs.statement: Create the Application and reserve usage atomically with the subquote acceptance. Payment and booking read the discounted price from the acceptance snapshot and never revalidate or recompute it.

nodes.title: Treatment changes never change the accepted promotion

nodes.title: Simultaneous code attempts on one subquote: the last confirmed wins and both are audited

nodes.title: If the code is no longer valid at confirmation, the patient may accept at the offered price or cancel

nodes.title: Admin program form hides sections that do not apply to the program type

nodes.title: Drilling from an Overview KPI card filters the Applications tab

nodes.title: Auto-applied mode on a Both-Fees program is rejected with an inline error

nodes.title: Bulk Revoke of selected codes requires a mandatory reason

nodes.title: Entry points to search and filter

attrs.statement: Patient Platform: [P2] Provider Search is accessed when the patient begins the quote request flow and needs to select destination/providers, is triggered from the "Choose Destination" or "Select Providers" screens, and is available throughout the quote request journey for comparison; [P2] Messaging search is accessed from the patient communications inbox once FR-012 messaging is scheduled; [P1] Help & Support search is accessed from the Help & Support hub, Help Center, and My Support Tickets screens. Provider Platform: PR-01 (Team) from Provider Dashboard → Team tab → Team Directory (FR-009/Screen 10); PR-02 (Inquiries/Quotes) from Provider Dashboard → Inquiries tab → Inquiry List (FR-003/Screen 9) and Quotes List (FR-004/Screen 2); PR-03 (Treatment) from Provider Dashboard → Treatments tab → In Progress Cases (FR-010/Screen 3); PR-04 (Aftercare) from Provider Dashboard → Aftercare tab → Aftercare Cases List (FR-011/Screen 8); PR-05 (Analytics) from Provider Dashboard → Analytics tab → Analytics Dashboard (FR-014/Screen 1); PR-06 (Profile/Settings) from Provider Dashboard → Profile/Settings section — Packages (FR-024/Screen 4), Help Centre (FR-032/Screen 5), Reviews (FR-032/Screen 1 Tab 5), Support Cases (FR-032/Screen 5.7); PR-07 (Messaging) [P2 - Post-MVP] from the provider secure messaging inbox once FR-012 is scheduled. Admin Platform [P1 - MVP]: each admin module (A-01 through A-10) provides context-specific search and filtering within its own interface.
attrs.rationale: Entry Points (prd.md lines 86-110). Business Process Assumption 3: patient searches for providers occur during the quote request flow, not as standalone exploration [P2]. Change log 2.7 removed admin global/cross-module search entry points.

nodes.title: Keyword and filters evaluated together in real time

attrs.statement: Search and filter controls are available simultaneously; the System evaluates the active keyword AND active filters together in real-time (Main Flow 1 admin patient search, Main Flow 2 admin provider search). In patient provider discovery the System evaluates destination, keyword, and filters together in real-time (Main Flow 3 [P2 - Post-MVP]).
attrs.rationale: Main Flows 1-3 CTRL and QUERY nodes (prd.md lines 127-188).

nodes.title: Default list and reset per search flow

attrs.statement: Admin opens Patients module — full patient list shown by default; Reset all clears all inputs and restores the full patient list (Main Flow 1). Admin opens Providers module — Active providers shown by default (FR-015 Screen 1); Reset all restores the default Active-only list (Main Flow 2). Patient Reset all clears all inputs and restores the full country list (Main Flow 3 [P2 - Post-MVP]).
attrs.rationale: Main Flows 1-3 NAV and RESET nodes (prd.md lines 124-199). FR-015 / Screen 1 Status filter default Active (line 1140).

attrs.statement: When a search term or filter combination matches no records, the System displays 'No results found' with refinement guidance: check spelling or try different keywords; remove one or more filters; contact support (admin platform only). In patient provider discovery the System displays 'No providers found' with refinement guidance.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B1 (prd.md lines 275-295); Main Flows 1-3 EMPTY nodes.

nodes.title: Search unavailable: message, retry, engineering alert

attrs.statement: If the backend database connection fails during a search query, the System displays 'Search temporarily unavailable. Please try again.', logs the error and alerts the engineering team; the user can retry, abandon the search or contact support.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B2 (prd.md lines 296-315).

attrs.statement: Search Inactive (default; no input in search field): placeholder text shown; full default list visible; no query fired; dimmed placeholder text and neutral input border. Search Active (user types in search field): typed text visible; clear (×) button appears; debounced query fires (300–500ms per screen spec); list filters to matching results; active input border. These states apply uniformly to every screen; any screen-specific deviation is noted inline under that screen.
attrs.rationale: Control Behavior Standards table rows Search Inactive and Search Active (prd.md lines 394-395).

nodes.title: Filter control states and reset to defaults

attrs.statement: Filter Inactive (default; no filters applied): filter button neutral; no filter chips; default query runs; full result set shown. Filter Active (one or more filter controls changed from default): active filter chips shown below filter bar; filter button highlighted; AND-logic applied across all active filters; list narrows; result count updates. Reset Filter (user taps "Clear Filters" / "Reset" / selects default option): all filter controls return to their default values; chips cleared; all filter parameters cleared; default result set restored; filter icon returns to neutral.
attrs.rationale: Control Behavior Standards table rows Filter Inactive, Filter Active and Reset Filter (prd.md lines 396-398). Related: REQ-022-008, REQ-022-054, REQ-022-055, REQ-022-056.

attrs.statement: AND logic applies across different active filter types simultaneously — a result must satisfy all active filter conditions at once. Within a single multi-select filter field, selected values are combined with OR logic — a result matches if it satisfies any of the selected values for that field.
attrs.rationale: Control Behavior Standards Filter Logic Note (line 400); change log 2.3 item 4.

nodes.title: Search and filter criteria: Provider Selection (FR-003 / Screen 7a) [P2]

attrs.statement: FR-003 / Screen 7a: Provider Selection [P2 — Post-MVP]. Patient searches for and selects providers during the quote request flow. Search: Provider name / keyword (Type: text; Placeholder: "Search providers…"; Debounce: 500ms; Max Length: 50 chars; Notes: Case-insensitive; matches provider name and specialty tags). Filters: Country / Destination (Type: Multi-select chips; Options: Patient's previously selected destination countries; Default: All selected countries; Logic: AND within selection) / Rating (Type: Star selector; Options: All, 4+ stars, 4.5+ stars; Default: All; Logic: Min threshold) / Specialty (Type: Dropdown; Options: Hair Transplant, Beard Transplant, Both; Default: All; Logic: Exact match) / Active Status (Type: Segmented; Options: All, Active Only; Default: Active Only; Logic: Single selection) / Available Capacity (Type: Toggle; Options: Show providers with open appointment slots only; Default: Off; Logic: Single flag).
attrs.rationale: Screen Specifications (prd.md lines 414-437). Screen owned by FR-003 (Patient tenant, Master Reference Table). Search inputs and filter controls are UI controls, not Fields; FR-022 owns the criteria (Maintenance Convention, line 319). Graph screen: SCR-003-08.

nodes.title: Subquote price sort basis, tie-break and ineligible placement

attrs.statement: Price sorts use each subquote's complete offered price as shown on FR-005 / Screen 1, with any promotion already included; the standard price before promotion and the price per graft are not used for price sorting. For ordering only, each price is converted to the patient's display currency at the current rate; each card still shows its own quote currency, and when the listed subquotes use more than one currency the price order is labelled approximate. Subquotes with the same sort value are ordered by parent quote send date (most recent first), then by option order within the parent quote, then by date range start. Subquotes that cannot currently be accepted (Not Selected, Expired, Withdrawn or Cancelled) stay in the list, shown disabled as in FR-005, and sort after all eligible subquotes. Each list row and each counted result is one subquote.
attrs.rationale: FR-005 / Screen 1 Sort basis paragraph (line 457). Restated by User Story 5 scenarios 1, 3, 4 and 5. Overlaps REQ-022-058 and REQ-005-027 on currency conversion.

Filters: Status (Type: Multi-select; Options: Open, In Progress, Closed, On Hold, Escalated; Default: Open + In Progress; Logic: OR (within field)) / Priority (Type: Multi-select; Options: High, Medium, Low; Default: All; Logic: OR (within field)) / Category (Type: Dropdown; Options: All; admin-defined ticket categories; Default: All; Logic: Exact match) / Ticket Source (Type: Dropdown; Options: All, Patient App, Provider App, Admin Portal; Default: All; Logic: Exact match) / Submitter Type (Type: Dropdown; Options: All, Patient, Provider; Default: All; Logic: Exact match) / Date Range (Type: Date range picker; Options: Custom; Default: Last 30 days; Logic: Filters by ticket creation date) / Assigned Admin (Type: Dropdown; Options: All; admin user list; Default: All; Logic: Exact match).
attrs.rationale: Screen Specifications (prd.md lines 1766-1791). Screen owned by FR-034 (Admin tenant, Master Reference Table). Search inputs and filter controls are UI controls, not Fields; FR-022 owns the criteria (Maintenance Convention, line 319).

nodes.title: Fuzzy, accent-insensitive matching via full-text indexes

attrs.statement: Search functionality MUST support fuzzy matching via database full-text indexes (e.g., "Mark P" matches "Mark Patterson"; "Mehmet" matches "Mehmet Yilmaz"; accent-insensitive matching, e.g., "Jose" matches "José").
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 2 (line 1797). Restated by Edge Case 4 (accent-insensitive matching, José matches Jose). Refines REQ-022-007. Advanced fuzzy features (synonyms, edit distance, relevance) are a P3 external-search enhancement.

nodes.title: Filter selections persist for the session

attrs.statement: Filter selections MUST persist during user session (cleared on logout)
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 4 (line 1799).

attrs.statement: Autocomplete suggestions MUST be limited to 10 results to avoid overwhelming user
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 7 (line 1802). Admin Editability Rules list the autocomplete result limit (10 suggestions) as fixed in codebase. REQ-022-015 applies the same limit to P2 location autocomplete.

attrs.statement: Search history MUST NOT be stored (privacy consideration for admin platform)
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 8 (line 1803). See needs-decision item on admin search audit logging (REQ-022-023, REQ-022-027).

nodes.title: Patient contact information not indexed for public search

attrs.statement: Patient contact information MUST NOT be indexed for public search (admin only)
attrs.rationale: Data & Privacy Rule 3 (line 1810).

nodes.title: Provider financial data not searchable by other providers

attrs.statement: Provider financial data MUST NOT be searchable by other providers (admin only)
attrs.rationale: Data & Privacy Rule 4 (line 1811).

nodes.title: Featured providers curated by admin; affects Recommended sort

attrs.statement: Featured provider designation is a manually curated list editable by admin; admin can feature/unfeature providers in patient search, affecting "Recommended" sort order.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules: Editable by Admin (line 1820) and Configurable with Restrictions (line 1833). Business Process Assumption 4: Featured status is manually curated by admin based on performance, quality, and partnerships. FR-015 / Screen 1 Featured filter.

nodes.title: Only active providers appear in search; suspension hides, never deletes

attrs.statement: Provider visibility status: active providers appear in search, suspended do not. Admin can temporarily disable provider from search results (suspension) but cannot delete provider record.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules: Editable by Admin (line 1821) and Configurable with Restrictions (line 1832).

nodes.title: Debounce timing fixed: 300ms local, 500ms server query

attrs.statement: Search debounce timing is fixed in codebase (not editable): per REQ-022-012, 300ms for local filters, 500ms for server-query searches.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules: Fixed in Codebase (line 1825).

nodes.title: Search query maximum length by platform

attrs.statement: Search query max length is fixed in codebase (not editable): 200 chars for admin, 200 chars for provider, 50 chars for patient.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules: Fixed in Codebase (line 1828); change log 2.3 item 3 and 2.5 item 5. See needs-decision item on screens that set 100 chars.

nodes.title: No active providers in the selected country [P2]

attrs.statement: When a patient searches for providers in a country with no active providers, the System displays "No providers available in [country]. Please try another location or contact support." with link to support chat.
attrs.rationale: Edge Case 1 (prd.md lines 2135-2136).

nodes.title: Many results: first page, total count and narrowing banner

attrs.statement: When an admin search matches very many records (e.g., a very common name), the System displays the first page of results (25 per page, per REQ-022-006) with total result count shown (e.g., "500+ results found") and an informational banner: "Many results found. Use filters to narrow down by location, status, or patient ID."
attrs.rationale: Edge Case 2 (prd.md lines 2138-2139); change log 2.4 item 2 (pagination is the single model; no truncation).

attrs.statement: Search times out after 10 seconds; error message displayed: "Search taking too long. Please try again or contact support."; error logged for engineering team to investigate.
attrs.rationale: Edge Case 5 (prd.md lines 2147-2148); the missing-index cause is technical and not migrated.

nodes.title: Duplicate patient accounts all returned and flagged

attrs.statement: When a patient has multiple accounts with the same name/email, search returns all matching accounts; the admin reviews each record to identify the correct patient using patient ID, location, or registration date; duplicate account detection is flagged in results.
attrs.rationale: Edge Case 7 (prd.md lines 2153-2154).

nodes.title: Patient email and phone shown only to authorised admins

attrs.statement: Patient PII (email, phone) displayed only to authorized admins with proper permissions
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Security Considerations: Data masking (line 2039); promoted as a business rule. Permissions per FR-031.

nodes.title: Complex filters run in a single database query

attrs.statement: Complex filters (multi-criteria) MUST execute in single database query (no N+1 queries)
attrs.rationale: Search Performance Rules, Rule 5 (line 1841).

nodes.title: Admin search logs retained for audit

attrs.statement: Admin search logs MUST be retained for audit purposes (who searched for whom, when)
attrs.rationale: Privacy Rule 2 (line 1809). REQ-022-023 requires the entry to be written; this rule requires it to be kept.

nodes.title: Database collation utf8mb4_unicode_ci for accent-insensitive search

attrs.statement: Search performs accent-insensitive matching (José matches Jose); database collation set to utf8mb4_unicode_ci (MySQL 8.0+).
attrs.rationale: Edge Case 4 (lines 2144-2145). Adds the collation to REQ-022-124.

nodes.title: Concurrent admin searches read a consistent snapshot

attrs.statement: Database read locks prevent conflicts; each admin sees consistent snapshot of patient data; audit logs capture each admin's search independently.
attrs.rationale: Edge Case 6 (lines 2150-2151).

nodes.title: Medical records retained 7 years; no hard-delete before expiry

attrs.statement: System MUST retain patient medical records for a minimum of 7 years; hard-deletion is prohibited before expiry.
attrs.rationale: Restated by Assumptions (7-year minimum applies to medical and financial records platform-wide unless stricter jurisdictional rules exist) and the Executive Summary (minimum 7 years for medical and financial records).

nodes.title: Financial records retained 7 years; no hard-delete before expiry

attrs.statement: System MUST retain financial transaction records for a minimum of 7 years; hard-deletion is prohibited before expiry.

nodes.title: Soft-delete only for protected categories, including cancelled inquiries and cascade records

attrs.statement: System MUST support soft-deletes only for protected categories (medical, financial, identity), preserving recoverability and auditability. Patient-cancelled inquiries (FR-003 Workflow 5) and all records generated from the cancellation cascade — including auto-cancelled quotes with status "Cancelled (Inquiry Cancelled)" per FR-004 — are subject to the same retention rules as completed inquiries and quotes. They are soft-deleted/archived, never hard-deleted before the retention period expires. This applies to inquiry records, quote records, acceptance events (including superseded AcceptanceEvents per FR-005), and associated audit trail entries.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Executive Summary (soft-deletion only for critical data) and Success Criteria (0% of critical records, medical and financial, hard-deleted before end of retention). The protected categories list names identity, which the REQ-023-009 category list does not; see the migration report.

nodes.title: Deletion request: non-protected data deleted or anonymized; protected records retained with restricted access

attrs.statement: System MUST allow patients to request data deletion (erasure); non-protected data is deleted or anonymized; protected medical/financial records are retained without anonymization but with strict access restrictions and documented legal basis.
attrs.rationale: Restated by Main Flow step 4 (system performs deletion or anonymization for non-protected data and restricts access to protected records), Clarification CL-1 (retain medical and financial records without anonymization but fully restrict access during the legal retention period; document legal basis in outcomes) and Success Criteria (no anonymization for retained medical or financial records). User Story 1 acceptance scenario 1 says protected records are "restricted/anonymized"; the graph follows this requirement, CL-1 and the success criteria.

nodes.title: Patient data anonymized in analytics and reports

attrs.statement: System MUST anonymize patient data in analytics and reports (no direct identifiers, quasi-identifiers masked or aggregated).
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Executive Summary (anonymizes patient data used in analytics) and Success Criteria (0% personally identifiable patient attributes in analytics dashboards or reports).

nodes.title: Audit log of all read and write access to protected records

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain audit logs for all read and write access to protected records, including actor, timestamp, object, action, outcome.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Executive Summary (audit logs for all data access and modification events), Success Criteria (100% of read/write access captured with who, when, what) and User Story 2 (a view of a medical record records who, when, what and outcome; a saved modification also records before/after metadata and the actor).

nodes.title: Admin views for retention configuration and DSR queues

attrs.statement: System MUST provide Admin views to configure retention by data category and jurisdiction and to manage DSR queues.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Admin Platform scope (configure retention settings by data category and region; triage and fulfill deletion requests).

nodes.title: Patients and Admins notified of DSR status updates and outcomes

attrs.statement: System MUST notify Patients and Admins about DSR status updates and completion outcomes.
System MUST classify data into categories: Medical Records, Financial Records, Communications, Media, Account Profile, Analytics.

nodes.title: Each category has a retention policy and legal basis, with jurisdiction overrides

attrs.statement: Each category MUST have an assigned retention policy and legal basis (with jurisdiction overrides).
attrs.rationale: Restated by Key Entities (Retention Policy: data category, default retention, legal basis, jurisdiction overrides).

nodes.title: Audit log entries immutable and retained at least 7 years

attrs.statement: Audit log entries MUST be immutable and retained for at least 7 years.
attrs.rationale: Restated by Clarification CL-3 (retain audit logs for 7 years; logs are immutable and included in compliance reporting). Other FRs state 10 years for their audit logs; see the migration report.

nodes.title: Backups every 6 hours, 30-day retention, deleted personal data excluded beyond window

attrs.statement: Backups MUST occur at least every 6 hours with 30-day retention (per system PRD) and exclude already-deleted personal data beyond backup windows.
attrs.rationale: Restated by Assumptions (backups every 6 hours with 30-day retention per system PRD; deleted data may persist in backups until window expiry).

nodes.title: Deletion purges search indexes and caches

attrs.statement: Deletion actions MUST purge search indexes and caches for impacted personal data.

nodes.title: Anonymization removes direct identifiers and reduces re-identification risk

attrs.statement: Anonymization MUST remove direct identifiers and reduce re-identification risk for quasi-identifiers.

nodes.title: Analytics consent captured and opt-outs honored

attrs.statement: System MUST capture consent for analytics usage where applicable and honor opt-outs in non-essential analytics.

nodes.title: Admin export of audit logs and retention reports in portable formats

attrs.statement: Provide Admin export of audit logs and retention reports in portable, non-proprietary formats.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Communication Structure (compliance reporting exports downloadable by Admin) and Clarification CL-3 (audit logs included in compliance reporting, summaries unless otherwise requested).

nodes.title: Programmatic DSR submission and status for the Patient app

attrs.statement: Provide programmatic access for DSR submission/status for Patient app integration.

nodes.title: DSR lifecycle events notified to internal communication channels

attrs.statement: Provide event notifications for DSR lifecycle events to internal communication channels.

nodes.title: Entry points to deletion, data policy, audit logs and retention settings

attrs.statement: Entry points: Patient: Profile/Privacy screen → Request Deletion. Provider: Settings → Data Policy (read-only); Activity Logs. Admin: Compliance dashboard → Retention Settings; DSR Queue; Audit Logs; Reports.
attrs.rationale: The PRD gives no Screen Specifications. The patient entry is the Delete Account screen SCR-001-16 (FR-001) and the admin DSR queue is SCR-016-08 (FR-016); the provider and admin compliance screens have no node yet.

nodes.title: Patients can view the retention policy, request deletion and receive status updates

attrs.statement: Patients can view the retention policy, request account/data deletion, and receive status updates and outcomes.

nodes.title: Providers can view the applicable retention and privacy policy

attrs.statement: Providers can view the applicable retention/privacy policy.

nodes.title: Providers cannot permanently delete protected records

attrs.statement: Providers cannot permanently delete protected records.

nodes.title: Providers have a read-only audit trail of their users' activity

attrs.statement: Providers have read-only access to the audit trail of activity by their users.

nodes.title: Admins can review audit trails of access and modifications to protected records

attrs.statement: Admins can review audit trails of access to and modifications of protected records, to investigate incidents and demonstrate compliance.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Admin Platform scope (review audit trails) and User Story 2 (a complete audit trail so an Admin can investigate incidents and demonstrate compliance).

attrs.statement: Admins can approve exceptions.
attrs.rationale: The PRD states this once in the Admin Platform scope and does not say which rules admit an exception; see the migration report.

nodes.title: Retention enforced by scheduled jobs from the retention policy

attrs.statement: Retention is enforced by cross-cutting scheduled jobs that apply the Retention Policy of each data category to records.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Shared Services scope (cross-cutting job scheduling for retention enforcement) and Key Entities (Retention Policy is applied to records via category mapping and referenced by enforcement jobs).

nodes.title: Module boundary: no chat or video, no payment flow changes, no DPO tooling

attrs.statement: Out of scope for this module: real-time chat/video features (managed by other modules), payment flow changes beyond record retention, and third-party DPO/legal tooling integrations (future consideration).

nodes.title: Patient notified at each DSR status change

attrs.statement: Patients are notified of each DSR status change: submission, verification required, in progress, and fulfilled.

nodes.title: Admins notified of new DSRs and approaching deadlines

attrs.statement: Admins are notified of new DSRs and of approaching deadlines.

nodes.title: Deletion request submitted from the Privacy screen and verified

attrs.statement: A patient submits a deletion request from the Privacy screen and completes verification.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Main Flow trigger (patient requests deletion from the Privacy screen) and Assumptions (patients are willing and able to complete identity verification for DSRs by standard methods).

nodes.title: System classifies the patient's data by category, retention and jurisdiction

attrs.statement: System classifies the patient's data by category and applicable retention/jurisdiction when a deletion request is processed.

nodes.title: Admin reviews the classification and approves the action

attrs.statement: Admin reviews the classification and approves the action before deletion, anonymization or restriction is performed.
attrs.rationale: Restated by User Story 1 acceptance scenario 1 (a verified deletion request is acted on when approved by Admin).

nodes.title: Deletion actions audit-logged; outcome notice lists actions and legal basis

attrs.statement: System records deletion actions in the audit log and notifies the patient of the outcome, listing the actions taken and the legal basis and scope of any retained categories.
attrs.rationale: Restated by Main Flow step 5, Alternative Flow A2 step 2 (the legal basis and scope of retained categories are included in the outcome notification) and User Story 1 acceptance scenario 2 (the notification lists actions taken and the legal basis for retained records).

nodes.title: Insufficient identity proof flags the request Verification Required

attrs.statement: A deletion request that lacks sufficient identity proof is flagged Verification Required and the patient is notified; the patient provides additional verification and an Admin validates it and resumes processing.
The deletion request SLA clock pauses during verification.
attrs.rationale: The 30-calendar-day completion target is stated in Success Criteria and already held as REQ-001-094 (FR-001); only the pause is new here. A1 line 82 says "Export/deletion proceeds" while line 83 says deletion only; export was removed in PRD version 1.3 and the graph follows line 83.

nodes.title: Admin confirms exclusion of protected medical and financial records

attrs.statement: When data categories include records subject to mandatory retention, an Admin confirms the exclusion of protected medical/financial records; deletion/anonymization completes for the non-protected data.

nodes.title: Concurrent DSRs merged or queued; SLA per consolidated request

attrs.statement: When a patient submits multiple DSRs concurrently, the system merges or queues them with a clear status; the SLA applies per consolidated request.

nodes.title: Deletion paused while an active booking exists

attrs.statement: When a patient requests deletion while an active booking exists, the system pauses deletion until the booking resolves and communicates the timeline.

nodes.title: Jurisdiction conflict defaults to stricter retention and flags Admin review

attrs.statement: On a jurisdiction conflict (for example EU versus non-EU residency), the system defaults to the stricter retention and flags the request for Admin review.
attrs.rationale: Restated by Assumptions (the 7-year minimum applies platform-wide unless stricter jurisdictional rules exist).

nodes.title: Deletion after inquiry cancellation proceeds; cancelled records stay retained

attrs.statement: A deletion request made after the patient cancelled an inquiry proceeds normally, because a cancelled inquiry is a terminal state with no active obligation. Cancelled inquiry records, cascaded cancelled quotes, and associated audit entries are retained per REQ-023-003 (7-year minimum for medical/financial data) even after PII anonymization; the anonymization applies to profile data, not to the retained medical/financial records.
System MUST allow admins to create treatments with name, type, description, video, images, and technique specifications
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 930).

nodes.title: Admin edits create new treatment versions

attrs.statement: System MUST allow admins to edit existing treatments, creating new versions without modifying historical records
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 931).

attrs.statement: System MUST allow admins to activate or deactivate treatments, affecting availability for new quotes only
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 932).

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to view all active treatments from admin catalog
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 933).

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to configure pricing for treatments they want to offer (base price, price per graft, graft ranges)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 934).

nodes.title: Providers enable or disable offerings without losing pricing

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to enable or disable treatment offerings without deleting pricing configuration
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 935).

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to create packages with name, description, included items, included travel services, relative-day treatment plan, standard price, images, and status (Active or Inactive)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 936).

nodes.title: Package edit creates a new version

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to edit existing packages in the package library; each save MUST create a new package version (v1, v2, and so on), keep earlier versions read-only, and never change existing quotes
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 937).

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to deactivate packages, hiding them from new quotes while preserving existing quotes
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 938).

nodes.title: Quote selects one treatment and one to five packages

attrs.statement: System MUST allow providers to select one treatment for the parent quote and one to five Active packages when creating quotes, where each selected package seeds exactly one alternative quote option
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 939).

nodes.title: Package standard price prefills each date-range row

attrs.statement: System MUST prefill each date-range price row of a package-seeded quote option with that package's standard price and MUST NOT sum package prices into one option total
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 940).

nodes.title: Quote keeps exact treatment and package versions

attrs.statement: System MUST retain the exact Treatment ID/version on the parent Quote and each selected Package ID/version as provenance on its Quote Option snapshot to prevent retroactive changes
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 941).

nodes.title: Treatment records are versioned and immutable

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain versioned treatment records with immutable history (no update-in-place)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 951).

nodes.title: Package records are versioned and immutable

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain versioned package records with immutable history, including each version's included items, travel services, and relative-day plan
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 952).

nodes.title: Media stored in object storage with CDN delivery

attrs.statement: System MUST store media files (videos, images) in S3-compatible object storage with CDN delivery
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 953).

nodes.title: Track which providers offer which treatments

attrs.statement: System MUST track which providers offer which treatments (provider-treatment pricing configuration)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 954).

nodes.title: Packages are owned by a provider account

attrs.statement: System MUST link packages to provider accounts (package ownership)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 955).

nodes.title: Historical quotes and bookings keep exact versions

attrs.statement: System MUST preserve the exact Treatment version and Quote Option package snapshots used in historical quotes and bookings
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 956).

nodes.title: Only admins create or edit treatments

attrs.statement: System MUST restrict treatment creation/editing to admin users only
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 960).

nodes.title: Providers manage only their own packages

attrs.statement: System MUST restrict package management to provider users (edit only their own packages)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 961).

nodes.title: Media served over TLS 1.3 through CDN

attrs.statement: System MUST serve media files via CDN over TLS 1.3 (HTTPS)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 962).

nodes.title: Treatment and package changes are audit-logged

attrs.statement: System MUST log all treatment and package modifications with timestamp, user ID, IP address, and old/new values
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 963).

nodes.title: Uploaded media validated for type, size and malware

attrs.statement: System MUST validate uploaded media files for type, size, and malicious content
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 964).

nodes.title: Providers cannot see other providers' packages

attrs.statement: System MUST prevent providers from viewing other providers' package catalogs
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 965).

nodes.title: REST API for treatment CRUD, admin only

attrs.statement: System MUST expose REST API for treatment CRUD operations (admin access only)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 969).

nodes.title: REST API for packages with no hard delete

attrs.statement: System MUST expose REST API for package create, read, update (new version), and deactivate operations, with no hard delete (provider access only)
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 970).

attrs.statement: System MUST integrate with S-05: Media Storage Service for video and image uploads
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 971).

attrs.statement: System MUST integrate with CDN service for media file delivery
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 972).

nodes.title: Integration with quote management for selection

attrs.statement: System MUST integrate with PR-02: Inquiry & Quote Management for treatment and package selection during quote creation
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 973).

nodes.title: Inline package edits stay in the quote

attrs.statement: System MUST keep inline package edits made during quote creation in that quote only and MUST NOT write them back to the library package or create a new package version
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 942).

nodes.title: Package holds no date range, notes or documents

attrs.statement: System MUST NOT store a date range, additional notes, or documents on a package; these are entered per inquiry in FR-004
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 943).

nodes.title: One system quote currency for all library prices

attrs.statement: System MUST use the system quote currency for all treatment and package library prices; providers MUST NOT choose a currency per treatment or package
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 944).

attrs.statement: System MUST NOT hard-delete packages; packages are deactivated or archived only
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 945).

nodes.title: Patients see package content from the option's own copy

attrs.statement: System MUST show patients package content only from the quote option's own copy or from the exact package version that option records, never from the latest library version
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 946).

nodes.title: Treatment base price is reference only

attrs.statement: System MUST treat the provider treatment Base Price as a reference-only, non-binding "starting from" value. It MAY prefill new FR-004 quote option/date-price rows only where no other standard value exists and MAY feed a future post-MVP starting price on provider cards; it MUST NOT be binding and MUST NOT be read after a quote is sent
attrs.rationale: Functional Requirements Summary (PRD line 947).

nodes.title: Patients only view treatment and package content

attrs.statement: Patients view treatment details (videos, descriptions, technique information) and each provider's package-based quote options within provider quotes, shown from the quote option's own copy, and compare offerings across provider quotes. Patients have no direct treatment or package management actions.
attrs.rationale: Stated in Multi-Tenant Breakdown, Patient Platform (PRD lines 33-36) and Patient Entry Points (View-Only).

nodes.title: Entry points to treatment and package management

attrs.statement: Admin reaches treatment management from "Settings > Treatment Settings" ("Create New Treatment", or edit from the treatment list). Provider reaches treatment pricing from "Products & Services > Treatments" ("Treatment Pricing") and the package catalog from "Products & Services > Packages" ("Create Package"). During quote creation the provider selects a treatment and one to five Active packages. Patients have view-only access through provider quotes.
attrs.rationale: Entry Points (PRD lines 80-100). User Story 1 scenario 3 (line 822) names "Settings > Treatment Pricing" for the provider path instead; this is an open product owner question question on navigation labels.

nodes.title: Treatments are one global catalog managed by admin

attrs.statement: All treatments are globally managed by admin and available to all active providers.
attrs.rationale: Business Rules, General Module Rule 1 (PRD line 530).

nodes.title: Admin can add new treatment types

attrs.statement: Admins define treatment types (FUE, FUT, DHI, Sapphire FUE, Robotic, Other) and can add new types to the treatment type list.
attrs.rationale: Admin scope (PRD line 52) and Admin Editability, Editable by Admin (line 570).

nodes.title: Admin views provider packages read-only for support

attrs.statement: Admin can view provider packages in read-only mode for support purposes only and cannot modify individual provider packages; provider ownership is enforced.
attrs.rationale: Admin scope (PRD lines 56-57), Privacy Rule 2 (line 557), Admin Editability, Configurable with Restrictions (line 582). The PRD specifies no admin screen for this view; this is an open product owner question question on the admin package view.

nodes.title: New treatment: all active providers notified

attrs.statement: When an admin saves a new treatment, System sends all active providers the notification "New treatment available in catalog", and providers can then configure pricing for it.
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure (PRD line 68); Main Flow steps 14-15 (lines 131-132); User Story 1.

nodes.title: Treatment update: providers who offer it notified

attrs.statement: When an admin updates a treatment, System notifies the providers who currently offer that treatment about the update (for example "Treatment [FUE] video has been updated").
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A1 step 9 (PRD line 148); User Story 5.

attrs.statement: When an admin deactivates a treatment, System notifies providers with the message "Treatment [Name] has been deactivated"; providers with active usage are notified.
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure (PRD line 69, providers with active usage) and Alternative Flow A2 step 8 (line 163, providers). The audience is an open product owner question; the graph holds the narrower Communication Structure reading.

nodes.title: Provider gets a confirmation after saving packages and pricing
