attrs.statement: Provider receives a confirmation when a package is created or updated ("Package created successfully", "Package saved successfully") and when treatment pricing is saved ("Treatment pricing saved successfully").
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure (PRD line 70); Main Flow: Provider Creates Package step 15 (line 246); Screen 3 notes (line 436); Screen 5 notes (line 522).

nodes.title: Treatment media formats and size limits

attrs.statement: A treatment video is optional, MP4 only, max 50MB. Treatment images are optional, JPEG or PNG, max 5 images of 5MB each. Educational resources are optional PDF documents, max 3 files of 10MB each. These limits and formats are fixed in the code, not admin-editable. A video over the limit is rejected with "Video file exceeds maximum size of 50MB. Please compress the video or upload a shorter version."
attrs.rationale: Main Flow steps 5-7 (PRD lines 122-124); Screen 2 fields (lines 370-372); Admin Editability, Fixed in Codebase (lines 572-574); Edge Cases (line 912); validation example B1 (lines 197-199).

nodes.title: Treatment save validates inputs and shows errors on the field

attrs.statement: On Save Treatment, System validates name uniqueness, required fields (name, type, description) and file formats. The name is unique across all treatments, max 100 characters. Description max 5,000 characters, technique specifications max 2,000, expected recovery time max 50, typical duration 0.5 to 12 hours. Errors are shown next to the invalid fields and the treatment is created only after validation passes.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow step 10 (PRD line 127); B1 (lines 188-206); Screen 2 fields and rules (lines 356-377).

nodes.title: Treatment needs at least one of description, video or images

attrs.statement: A treatment must have at least one of: description, video, or images.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 business rules (PRD line 378). The same table marks Description as required (line 366), so the two lines disagree; this is an open product owner question. The graph keeps both readings: ENT-treatment.description is required and this rule is recorded as written.

nodes.title: Treatment status is set by admin; only Active ones are visible to providers

attrs.statement: A treatment's status is Active or Inactive, set by the admin on the treatment form (default Active). Only Active treatments are visible to providers; Inactive treatments are hidden from provider view.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow steps 8 and 13 (PRD lines 125, 130); Screen 2 Status (line 373); Screen 3 rules (lines 420-421). Step 13 says the record is saved as Active; this is an open product owner question.

nodes.title: Failed media upload retries, then saves without media

attrs.statement: When a media upload to S-05 fails, System retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff. If all retries fail it shows an error ("Media upload failed, please try again"), saves the treatment record without media marked "Pending Media Upload", and the admin can retry the upload separately by editing the treatment; once the upload succeeds the record is updated.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B2 (PRD lines 208-218); Edge Cases (line 920).

nodes.title: Concurrent treatment edits use optimistic locking

attrs.statement: System uses optimistic locking with version timestamps on treatment edits. When a second admin saves a treatment another admin changed, System rejects the save with "This treatment was modified by another admin. Please refresh and reapply your changes." and the second admin must reload and reapply the edits.
attrs.rationale: Edge Cases (PRD line 922).

nodes.title: Treatment deactivation warns and needs admin confirmation

attrs.statement: Before deactivating a treatment, System checks the open quotes (draft or sent) and the open FR-006 bookings (Accepted, Confirmed, In Progress, Aftercare) that use it, shows a warning with the number of providers offering it and of active quotes, and requires the admin to confirm; on confirmation the status becomes Inactive.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A2 steps 2-6 (PRD lines 154-161); Screen 1 notes (line 351); Screen 2 rules (line 382). Screen 1 line 343 ("Deactivate button disabled if no active quotes exist using this treatment") contradicts A2 and is not recorded as a rule; this is an open product owner question.

nodes.title: Deactivated treatment cannot be picked for new quotes

attrs.statement: Providers cannot select a deactivated treatment in new quotes. If a treatment is deactivated while a provider has a draft quote open, System refreshes the available treatments and warns "Treatment [Name] is no longer available. Please select a different treatment." Existing quotes and bookings using the treatment continue unaffected.
attrs.rationale: A2 steps 7 and 9 (PRD lines 162, 165); Edge Cases (line 918). Whether a draft that already holds the treatment must change it is an open product owner question.

nodes.title: Treatments and packages are archived, never deleted; retention follows FR-023

attrs.statement: Treatments cannot be deleted: admins deactivate them (soft delete only). Deactivated treatments and packages are archived, not deleted, with the retention period governed by FR-023.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability, Configurable with Restrictions (PRD line 581); Data & Privacy Rules, Data Retention (line 561). REQ-024-033 covers packages never being hard-deleted.

nodes.title: Admin treatment list: order, search, filter, edit

attrs.statement: The admin treatment list shows Active treatments first and Inactive last, filters by treatment name in real time and by treatment type, shows "Create New Treatment" at all times, allows Edit on every treatment regardless of status, and shows 20 treatments per page.
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 business rules and notes (PRD lines 339-344, 352).

nodes.title: Number of Providers counts providers offering the treatment

attrs.statement: Number of Providers on the admin treatment list is the count of provider treatment pricing configurations for that treatment whose status is Offered. It is calculated, not entered.
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 field (PRD line 333) and Field Calculation Rules (line 629). Screen 1 rule at line 345 words it as providers who have configured pricing; this is an open product owner question.

nodes.title: Timestamps shown in local timezone; Last Updated is updated_at

attrs.statement: All timestamps are displayed in the provider's local timezone. Last Updated on every screen is the database updated_at timestamp, displayed in the user's local timezone.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 6 (PRD line 535) and Field Calculation Rules (line 631). Provider versus user timezone for admin screens is an open product owner question.

nodes.title: Draft auto-save and Cancel on the treatment and package forms

attrs.statement: The admin treatment form auto-saves a draft every 30 seconds to prevent data loss. The package form offers Save as Draft for an incomplete package. Cancel on either form discards unsaved changes and returns to the list.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 rules and notes (PRD lines 384, 391); Screen 5 rules and notes (lines 513, 521). A draft state is not in the status values; this is an open product owner question.

nodes.title: Providers see active treatments and a Not Configured badge

attrs.statement: Providers can only view active treatments from the admin catalog. A treatment the provider has not configured pricing for shows a "Not Configured" badge.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 business rules (PRD lines 420-422); A3 step 2 (line 175).

nodes.title: Pricing must be configured before a treatment is offered in quotes

attrs.statement: A provider must set a base price to enable "Offered" status and must configure pricing for a treatment before offering it in quotes. Saving the pricing configuration makes the treatment available in quote creation.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 rules (PRD lines 423, 428); Provider Editability (line 602); A3 steps 5 and 9 (lines 180, 184).

attrs.statement: System validates treatment pricing on save: no negative values; base price > 0; price per graft optional and >= 0 (some treatments are fixed price, not graft-based); minimum graft count > 0 and below the maximum; maximum graft count greater than minimum. A maximum below the minimum shows "Maximum graft count must be greater than minimum graft count." next to the maximum field.
attrs.rationale: A3 step 7 (PRD line 182); Screen 3 fields and rules (lines 416-419, 427); Edge Cases (line 916).

nodes.title: Providers set their own prices without admin approval

attrs.statement: Providers have authority to set their own treatment pricing and package prices without admin approval.
attrs.rationale: Business Process Assumption 2 (PRD line 753), promoted because it states who decides prices.

attrs.statement: Provider can copy a treatment's pricing configuration from another treatment with the "Quick Copy Pricing" option.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 notes (PRD line 435).

nodes.title: Package item types and travel services are fixed value lists

attrs.statement: Each included package item has a service type (medical, travel, accommodation, transport, flight, or other), a name, an optional description, an optional component price (>= 0), and an included flag. The service types are fixed in the code, aligned with FR-004. Included travel services are chosen from flight, hotel, transport, and other travel services.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow: Provider Creates Package steps 5-6 (PRD lines 236-237); Screen 5 fields (lines 491-492); Admin Editability, Fixed in Codebase (line 577).

nodes.title: Package plan uses relative days from Day 1

attrs.statement: A package's treatment plan uses relative days (Day 1, Day 2, and so on), each with a description, consecutive from Day 1; it never holds calendar dates.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow step 7 and step 12 (PRD lines 238, 243); Screen 5 field (line 493).

attrs.statement: On Save Package, System validates: name not empty (max 100); description required (max 2,000); standard price > 0 with up to 2 decimal places; at least one included item with an allowed service type and component price >= 0; plan days consecutive from Day 1 with a description; duration max 50 characters in common patterns ("X nights", "X days", "X hours", "X sessions"); terms max 1,000 characters. Errors are shown next to the invalid fields and the package is created only after validation passes.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow step 12 (PRD line 243); B3 (lines 299-313); Screen 5 fields and rules (lines 488-505).

nodes.title: Package needs at least one of description or images

attrs.statement: A package must have at least one of: description or images.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 notes (PRD line 519). The same table marks Description as required (line 490), so the two lines disagree; this is an open product owner question. The graph keeps both readings: ENT-package.description is required and this rule is recorded as written.

nodes.title: Package image formats and size limits

attrs.statement: Package images are optional, JPEG or PNG, max 3 images of 2MB each. The 2MB per-image limit is fixed in the code and not editable by providers. An image over the limit is rejected.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow step 8 (PRD line 239); Screen 5 field (line 496); Provider Editability, Fixed in Codebase (line 598); B3 (line 303).

nodes.title: Package name unique within the provider's catalog

attrs.statement: A package name must be unique within the provider's own package catalog and may repeat across providers. A duplicate name is rejected with "A package with this name already exists. Please choose a different name or edit the existing package."
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 rules (PRD line 503); Edge Cases (line 914).

nodes.title: A new package is version 1 and an Active one is selectable at once

attrs.statement: System saves a new package as version 1 linked to the provider account. Saving an Active package makes it immediately available in quote creation.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow step 14 and outcome (PRD lines 245, 247); Screen 5 rules (line 510).

nodes.title: New quote options copy the latest package version

attrs.statement: New quote options copy the latest version of the package.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A4 step 10 (PRD line 268).

nodes.title: No save-for-future from an inline package edit

attrs.statement: There is no "save for future" action from an inline package edit during quote creation. To reuse a change, the provider repeats it as a library edit in package management.
attrs.rationale: Package Edit Paths (PRD line 552).

nodes.title: Package deactivation warns of open quotes and needs confirmation

attrs.statement: Before deactivating a package, System counts the open quotes (draft or sent) that contain a quote option copied from the package, warns "This package is used in N open quotes. Deactivating hides it from new quotes; existing quotes are not changed.", and requires the provider to confirm; if the package is used in open quotes, confirmation is required. On confirmation the status becomes Inactive.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A5 steps 3-6 (PRD lines 278-281); Screen 4 rules (line 467); Screen 5 rules (line 512); User Story 6.

attrs.statement: Provider can clone an existing package. System creates a new package record copied from the original with "(Copy)" appended to the name; the provider edits the name, duration, and price and saves it.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A6 (PRD lines 286-297); Screen 4 rules (line 466).

nodes.title: Usage Count of open quote options

attrs.statement: Usage Count on the package list is the number of FR-004 quote options copied from any version of the package whose parent quote is still open (status draft or sent). The deactivation warning shows the number of distinct open parent quotes among them. It is calculated, not entered.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 field (PRD line 456) and rule (line 468); Field Calculation Rules (line 630).

nodes.title: Included Items summary shows first three items

attrs.statement: The package list shows a short summary of the included items: the first 3 items and "+N more". It is calculated, not entered.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 field Included Items (PRD line 451).

nodes.title: Provider package list: order, search, filter, sort

attrs.statement: The provider package list shows Active packages first and Inactive last, filters by package name in real time and by status, can be sorted by name, price, or usage count, shows "Create New Package" at all times, and shows 20 packages per page.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 business rules and notes (PRD lines 462-469, 476).

nodes.title: Bulk actions and quick price edit on the package list

attrs.statement: The package list offers the bulk actions "Deactivate Selected" and "Export to CSV". A quick price edit from the list is a library edit and saves a new package version.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 notes (PRD lines 475, 477).

nodes.title: No platform limit on packages per provider

attrs.statement: A provider can create unlimited packages; the platform imposes no limit.
attrs.rationale: Provider Editability, Business Rules for Providers (PRD line 604).

nodes.title: Package images only to patients viewing that provider's quote

attrs.statement: Package images are accessible only to patients viewing quotes from that provider, and are resolved from the package version recorded on the quote option.
attrs.rationale: Data & Privacy Rules, Privacy Rule 4 (PRD line 559).

nodes.title: Treatment media served by time-limited signed URLs

attrs.statement: Treatment videos and images are served via CDN using time-limited, signed URLs; unauthenticated bulk access is not allowed.
attrs.rationale: Data & Privacy Rules, Privacy Rule 3 (PRD line 558). External Dependencies line 704 describes a fallback to direct S3 URLs; this is an open product owner question.

nodes.title: Treatment and package text is translatable via FR-021

attrs.statement: Treatment descriptions and technique specifications, package names and descriptions, and all UI labels and error messages are translatable and use i18n keys from FR-021. Treatment type codes (FUE, FUT, DHI, Sapphire FUE, Robotic), package item service type codes, and media file names and CDN URLs stay in English. Before production release all treatment- and package-related strings must be registered with the FR-021 translation management system.
attrs.rationale: Localization Rules (PRD lines 607-623).

nodes.title: Provider staff role permissions gate package management

attrs.statement: Role-based permissions (FR-009) determine which provider staff can create and edit packages; package creation and editing are permission-checked by staff role.
attrs.rationale: Internal Dependencies, FR-009 (PRD lines 686-688). The permission matrix is owned by FR-009.

nodes.title: Package selection blocked when the package API is unavailable

attrs.statement: If the package API is temporarily unavailable, package selection is blocked with a retry message. System never seeds a quote option from cached data whose price or content does not match the package version it records.
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Integration 3 error handling (PRD line 786), promoted because it is a business rule inside a technical section.

nodes.title: Package erasure and export follow FR-023 and GDPR

attrs.statement: EU providers can export their package data (GDPR). Package erasure requests follow FR-023 retention rules because quote history references package versions.
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Security Considerations, Compliance (PRD line 803), promoted because it states an erasure and export obligation.

nodes.title: Context types are fixed in code

attrs.statement: Context types are system-defined (fixed in source code). Admins cannot create or delete context types; they assign one to each questionnaire set they create.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 rule (line 419): Admins cannot create, rename, or delete context types; changes to context type definitions require a code deployment

nodes.title: Context Type Reference screen is read-only

attrs.statement: This screen is entirely read-only; no fields are editable

nodes.title: Set carries a required Context Type and optional tags

attrs.statement: Each questionnaire set carries a required Context Type and optional tags (e.g., "pain", "sleep", "compliance"). Downstream modules filter the catalog by compatible Context Type when presenting assignment options.

nodes.title: Question context is inherited from its set

attrs.statement: System checks the parent set's Context Type (inherited — not chosen per question).
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 flow diagram, question configuration step.

nodes.title: Set is a named, versioned package with one Context Type

attrs.statement: Each questionnaire set is a named, versioned package of questions with a single Context Type

nodes.title: Publish needs at least one Active question

attrs.statement: A questionnaire set must contain at least one Active question before it can be published

nodes.title: Questions are ordered; order sets display sequence

attrs.statement: Questions within a set are ordered; order determines display sequence to patients
attrs.rationale: Also: Question order must be maintained during updates

nodes.title: Duplicate set creates an independent Draft copy

attrs.statement: Duplicating a set creates a Draft copy with all questions; the copy's Context Type is editable before first publish; the copy does not inherit the Inquiry designation
attrs.rationale: Business Rules 1 (line 496): A set may be duplicated to create a new Draft copy; the copy is independent of the source

nodes.title: Drag-and-drop reorder saves as Draft change

attrs.statement: Drag-and-drop reordering updates display order immediately and is saved as a Draft change
Question types are system-defined (fixed in source code); admin selects from the available type list but cannot create, rename, or remove types
attrs.rationale: Available system-defined types: Yes/No, Visual Scale 1–10, Numeric Scale 1–10, Multi-select, Free Text

nodes.title: Question Type locked after first save

attrs.statement: Question Type is locked after first save; changing type requires deleting and recreating the question
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 rule (line 362): Question Type is locked after first save; a confirmation dialog warns the admin before saving for the first time

nodes.title: Inquiry and Multi-Context questions need severity flag and Yes detail prompt

attrs.statement: Questions in Inquiry or Multi-Context sets: Severity Flag is required; Yes-answer detail prompt is required for Yes/No questions
attrs.rationale: Screen 3: Severity Flag and Alert Description are shown only if the parent set's Context Type is Inquiry or Multi-Context (line 355); Detail Prompt is required for Yes/No questions in those sets.

nodes.title: Publish blocked without a severity flag on every question

attrs.statement: All questions in Inquiry/Multi-Context sets must have a Severity flag before publishing
attrs.rationale: Severity flags must be assigned to all questions in Inquiry and Multi-Context sets Workflow 2: System enforces all questions in the set have a Severity Flag; blocks publish if any question is missing a flag.

nodes.title: MVP: Inquiry and Multi-Context sets are Yes/No only

attrs.statement: MVP: Inquiry and Multi-Context sets MUST contain only Yes/No questions; the system blocks publishing if any non-Yes/No questions exist
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 (line 316): MVP: Inquiry/Multi-Context sets can contain only Yes/No question types (enforced at publish-time) Screen 3 type validation: if parent set Context Type is Inquiry or Multi-Context, only Yes/No is selectable. Context-type table: MVP Yes/No only (hard constraint).

nodes.title: Future: typed answers in Inquiry sets once FR-003 supports them

attrs.statement: Future (V2+): Once FR-003 supports typed answers, Inquiry/Multi-Context sets may allow additional question types (with a publish-time warning)
attrs.rationale: Context-type table: additional question types allowed only after FR-003 supports typed answers.

nodes.title: Aftercare-only sets have no severity flags or alerts

attrs.statement: Aftercare-only questionnaire sets do not have severity flags and do not generate inquiry-style alerts
attrs.rationale: Context-type table: Aftercare supports all system-defined types; no severity flags.

nodes.title: Severity flags drive provider alerts for inquiry only

attrs.statement: Severity flags drive the automatic provider alert system for the inquiry flow only
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2 scope: severity flags and the provider alert system apply exclusively to Inquiry-context and Multi-Context sets.

attrs.statement: Critical questions: High-risk conditions (HIV, hepatitis, blood disorders, heart conditions) Standard questions: Moderate concerns (allergies, medications, chronic conditions) No Alert questions: General health status, lifestyle factors

nodes.title: No delivery frequency at question level

attrs.statement: Questions in Aftercare or Multi-Context sets: no frequency setting at question level — delivery frequency is configured in FR-011 at the milestone assignment step
attrs.rationale: Repeated at lines 318, 358, 561 and 572: Delivery frequency (how often the patient is prompted to complete the questionnaire at a given milestone) is configured in FR-011 at the milestone assignment level — not in FR-025 at the question level Frequency is not a question-level field; it is not validated here

nodes.title: Conditional question fields follow the question type

attrs.statement: Conditional fields (Detail Prompt, Scale Labels, Options, Placeholder, Max Characters) are shown or hidden dynamically based on the selected Question Type
attrs.rationale: Per-type requirements from the Screen 3 table: Scale Point Labels required for Visual Scale 1-10; Scale Min/Max Labels required for Numeric Scale 1-10; Options required for Multi-select (min 2 options); Placeholder Text and Max Characters optional for Free Text (Max Characters integer > 0).

attrs.statement: Question text must meet minimum length requirements
attrs.rationale: Screen 3: Question Text min 10 chars.

nodes.title: Duplicate question text in a set is prevented

attrs.statement: Duplicate question text within the same set must be prevented

nodes.title: Incomplete questions save as Inactive and skip publish validation

attrs.statement: Incomplete questions (required fields missing) save as Inactive and are excluded from publish validation
attrs.rationale: See needs-decision item 1: line 363 against lines 567 and 569 and the A4 publish-block step.

nodes.title: All questions pass completeness before publish

attrs.statement: All questions must pass completeness validation before the parent set can be published
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 alternative flow A4: Incomplete questions found: System blocks publish and lists incomplete questions.

attrs.statement: Every questionnaire set must be assigned a category before it can be published
attrs.rationale: The set must have a Category assigned before publishing A category must be assigned to the questionnaire set

nodes.title: Categories are global; one category per set

attrs.statement: Categories are global across all questionnaire sets
attrs.rationale: Each questionnaire set belongs to exactly one category Categories are used for organising and filtering the Questionnaire Catalog (Screen 1) Screen 4 (line 391): Each questionnaire set belongs to exactly one category

attrs.statement: Category names must be unique

nodes.title: Category delete blocked while sets are assigned

attrs.statement: Deleting a category with assigned sets is blocked; admin must first reassign those sets or deactivate the category

nodes.title: Category deactivation keeps assignments and flags sets Uncategorised

attrs.statement: Deactivating a category hides it from the category picker in Screen 2 but does not remove existing assignments; affected sets are flagged as "Uncategorised" until reassigned
attrs.rationale: Screen 2: Category must exist and be Active.

nodes.title: Category assignment consistent across catalog views

attrs.statement: Category assignment must be consistent across catalog views

nodes.title: Publish increments version and archives previous Active

attrs.statement: Publishing increments the version number and archives the previous Active version
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 publish step: System increments version, marks set as Active; archives previous Active version.

nodes.title: Editing a published set creates a Draft; Active keeps serving

attrs.statement: Changes to a question in an Active (published) set are saved as a Draft change on the parent set; the Active version continues to serve downstream consumers until the set is re-published
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 alternative flow A1 and Workflow 2 flow B1: the published Active version stays unchanged until the new Draft is published.

nodes.title: Context Type locked while set is Active

attrs.statement: Context Type cannot be changed while Status = Active; editing it creates a new Draft version automatically

nodes.title: Version activation needs explicit admin confirmation

attrs.statement: Version activation requires explicit admin confirmation

nodes.title: Changes require admin authentication and authorization

attrs.statement: Changes require admin authentication and authorization
attrs.rationale: Security Considerations (line 665): Strict admin-only access to questionnaire management.

nodes.title: All question changes are version controlled

attrs.statement: All question changes must be version controlled

nodes.title: Previous versions are archived, not deleted

attrs.statement: Previous versions must be archived, not deleted
Rollback capability must be available for all versions
attrs.rationale: Screen 7: "Restore as New Draft" creates a new Draft version of the set with the questions from the selected historical version; the currently Active version is not affected until the restored Draft is published

attrs.statement: "View Snapshot" opens a read-only view of the questionnaire set at that version; no editing is possible from the snapshot view

nodes.title: Version history and audit trail kept indefinitely and tamper-proof

attrs.statement: Version history and audit trail are maintained indefinitely and are tamper-proof
attrs.rationale: Audit logs must be retained for compliance requirements Audit trail must be tamper-proof and immutable

nodes.title: All admin actions on a set are audited

attrs.statement: All admin actions on the set — including metadata edits, question changes, and publish/archive events — are captured in the audit trail
attrs.rationale: All changes must be logged with timestamp and admin identification

nodes.title: Audit entries hold before and after values

attrs.statement: Audit trail must include before/after values for all modifications

nodes.title: Audit entries track IP address and session

attrs.statement: Security information (IP address, session) must be tracked

nodes.title: Question delete is soft; responses preserved

attrs.statement: Deleting a question performs a soft delete; historical patient responses referencing this question are preserved and remain accessible
attrs.rationale: Workflow 1 alternative flow A2: System soft-deletes question; historical patient responses are preserved.

nodes.title: Set in use cannot be deleted, only archived

attrs.statement: A set in use (designated for Inquiry or assigned to a milestone) cannot be deleted; it can only be Archived

nodes.title: Deleting a Draft set with no usages removes it

attrs.statement: Deleting a Draft set with no usages permanently removes it

nodes.title: Used In column shows usage locations

attrs.statement: Sets currently assigned to the inquiry flow or at least one milestone template display their usage locations in the "Used In" column

nodes.title: Archiving the active Inquiry set unconfigures the Inquiry flow

attrs.statement: Archiving a set that is currently designated as the active Inquiry questionnaire removes the designation and flags the inquiry flow as unconfigured; system notifies admin

nodes.title: Publishing does not activate a set for Inquiry

attrs.statement: Publishing does not activate a set for the inquiry flow. The admin must explicitly click "Set as Active for Inquiry" on a published Inquiry or Multi-Context set to designate it. This is a separate, deliberate action
attrs.rationale: Repeated in the Executive Summary, Entry Points, Workflow 1 outcome and Integration Rules.

nodes.title: At most one active Inquiry set; replacing needs confirmation

attrs.statement: At most one set may be designated as the active Inquiry questionnaire at a time. Clicking "Set as Active for Inquiry" on a second set shows a confirmation dialog and, upon confirmation, transfers the designation from the previous set to the new one
attrs.rationale: Workflow 4: System shows confirmation 'This will replace [Current Set Name] as the active Inquiry questionnaire. Continue?'; cancel leaves the previous set active; on confirm all new patient inquiry submissions (FR-003) use the new set immediately.

nodes.title: Set as Active for Inquiry only on published Inquiry or Multi-Context sets

attrs.statement: The "Set as Active for Inquiry" action is only available on sets with Status = Active (published) and Context Type = Inquiry or Multi-Context. It is hidden for Draft, Archived, and Aftercare-only sets
attrs.rationale: Workflow 4: for a Draft or Archived set the System blocks activation: 'Only published sets can be designated as the active Inquiry questionnaire'.

nodes.title: No active Inquiry set blocks submissions and warns admin

attrs.statement: If no set is designated as the active Inquiry questionnaire, the system must block patient inquiry submissions and display a system-level warning to admins
attrs.rationale: If no set is currently designated for the inquiry flow, the catalog displays a warning banner: "No active Inquiry questionnaire set — patient inquiry submissions will be blocked until one is designated" Workflow 4 (A2): System flags Inquiry flow as unconfigured; Notifies admin that no active Inquiry questionnaire is set; Patient inquiry submissions are blocked until a new set is designated.

nodes.title: Active Inquiry set delivered dynamically to inquiry submission

attrs.statement: The admin-designated active Inquiry questionnaire set must be delivered dynamically to the patient inquiry process; publishing a set does not make it the active Inquiry set — the admin must explicitly toggle "Set as Active for Inquiry"
attrs.rationale: System-Triggered (Inquiry): The admin-designated active Inquiry-context questionnaire set is delivered automatically during patient inquiry submission (FR-003). The active set is selected explicitly by the admin via the "Set as Active for Inquiry" toggle on the Questionnaire Catalog — publishing alone does not activate a set for the inquiry flow

nodes.title: Entry points to questionnaire management and delivery

attrs.statement: Admin-Initiated: Primary flow through the Questionnaire Catalog (Screen 1) System-Triggered (Inquiry): The admin-designated active Inquiry-context questionnaire set is delivered automatically during patient inquiry submission (FR-003). The active set is selected explicitly by the admin via the "Set as Active for Inquiry" toggle on the Questionnaire Catalog — publishing alone does not activate a set for the inquiry flow System-Triggered (Aftercare): Questionnaire set assigned to a milestone delivered according to the milestone schedule (FR-011) System-Triggered (Monitoring Advice): The same admin-designated active Inquiry-context questionnaire set is delivered when a patient activates provider-advice mode on a hair-loss monitoring case (FR-037), gating provider access rather than inquiry submission. No separate context type or admin toggle is introduced; FR-037 reuses the existing active Inquiry-context set as-is Provider-Viewed: Inquiry alert summaries and aftercare response data displayed in provider platform

nodes.title: Monitoring advice reuses the active Inquiry set

attrs.statement: System-Triggered (Monitoring Advice): The same admin-designated active Inquiry-context questionnaire set is delivered when a patient activates provider-advice mode on a hair-loss monitoring case (FR-037), gating provider access rather than inquiry submission. No separate context type or admin toggle is introduced; FR-037 reuses the existing active Inquiry-context set as-is
Version consistency must be maintained across all platforms
attrs.rationale: Questionnaire version must be consistent across all platforms

nodes.title: Version mismatch pushes current Active version and restarts patient

attrs.statement: Version mismatch detected (C1): System pushes current Active version to patient platform. Patient app reloads with updated questionnaire. Patient re-completes from the start if already in progress.

nodes.title: Questionnaire version recorded against each inquiry

attrs.statement: System records the questionnaire version number against this specific inquiry.

nodes.title: Responses, alert outcome and version are logged to the audit trail

attrs.statement: System logs all responses, alert outcome, and questionnaire version to audit trail.
Question formatting must be optimized for mobile devices

nodes.title: Validation consistent between admin and patient platforms

attrs.statement: Validation rules must be consistent between admin and patient platforms

nodes.title: Error handling gives clear user guidance

attrs.statement: Error handling must provide clear user guidance

nodes.title: Medical alerts generated automatically from responses

attrs.statement: Medical alerts must be generated automatically from questionnaire responses
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2: Alert rules derived automatically from Severity Flags — no extra configuration needed.

nodes.title: Alert tier from Critical, Standard and No answers

attrs.statement: Any Critical question answered Yes: System generates Red alert (highest risk). Otherwise, any Standard question answered Yes: System generates Yellow / Amber alert (moderate concern). Otherwise, all answered No: System generates Green indicator (no medical concerns flagged). System delivers the alert to the Provider Platform; the alert level is shown on the inquiry view.
attrs.rationale: Workflow 2 and Workflow 3 flow diagrams (lines 129-139 and 169-179).

nodes.title: Alert severity matches question severity flag

attrs.statement: Alert severity must match question severity flags
attrs.rationale: Alert generation rules must match severity flag assignments Screen 3: for Yes/No questions with a Severity Flag, response color-coding in the provider view is automatic based on the flag value; no additional configuration is needed.

attrs.statement: Alert display must be consistent with color-coding standards
attrs.rationale: Providers must be able to quickly scan alerts (red/amber/green) in-portal

attrs.statement: Alert history must be maintained for provider reference

nodes.title: MVP: no extra email or push for alert severity

attrs.statement: MVP: No additional email/push notification is emitted solely due to medical alert severity; providers learn via standard inquiry notifications and in-portal alert indicators

nodes.title: Each milestone independently selects one Aftercare or Multi-Context set

attrs.statement: Each aftercare milestone independently selects one questionnaire set from the catalog, filtered to Context Type = Aftercare or Multi-Context

nodes.title: Different milestones may use different sets

attrs.statement: Different milestones within the same aftercare template may be assigned different questionnaire sets (e.g., Week 1 milestone → "Pain Assessment", Week 4 milestone → "Sleep Quality Check")

nodes.title: Inquiry sets cannot be assigned to aftercare milestones

attrs.statement: Questionnaire sets with Context Type = Inquiry are not selectable in aftercare milestone assignments
attrs.rationale: Workflow 4 (A3): System blocks assignment: 'Inquiry-only sets cannot be assigned to aftercare milestones'.

nodes.title: Changing a milestone set keeps earlier responses on their version

attrs.statement: Changing a milestone's assigned questionnaire set does not affect previously submitted patient responses; those remain linked to the version used at time of submission
attrs.rationale: Workflow 4 (A4): future deliveries use the new set; existing patient responses remain linked to the prior version.

attrs.statement: System must handle concurrent admin modifications gracefully
Preview reflects the current saved Draft state of the set (all pending changes included); it does not show the last published version
Test Mode submissions do not create any records; all inputs are discarded on exit

nodes.title: Preview scoped to one set, opened from Set Details

attrs.statement: Preview is scoped to one questionnaire set at a time; opened from Screen 2

nodes.title: Settings UI limited to Settings Manager and Settings Viewer

attrs.statement: System MUST provide Settings Management UI accessible only to admins with "Settings Manager" or "Settings Viewer" role
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 states a different permission name ("Settings Management"); see the open question on permission naming.

nodes.title: Change reason required for every setting change

attrs.statement: System MUST require change reason (10-500 characters) for all setting modifications
attrs.rationale: Restated by General Module Rule 1 and Main Flow step 9 (modal titled "Change Reason", 10-500 chars, shown after Save) and by the Screen Specification notes and the A1 to A9 workflows.

nodes.title: Setting changes versioned with auto-incremented numbers

attrs.statement: System MUST version all setting changes with auto-incremented version numbers (v1.0, v1.1, v1.2, etc.)
attrs.rationale: Restated by General Module Rule 2 and Main Flow step 11.

nodes.title: Immutable audit log entry for every change

attrs.statement: System MUST create immutable audit log for every change capturing: timestamp, admin ID, admin email, setting group, old values, new values, change reason
attrs.rationale: Restated by Audit Rule 1, Audit Rule 2 (no deletion, no editing) and Main Flow step 10; Screen 7 states that version history is immutable.

nodes.title: Changes propagate within 1 minute by polling

attrs.statement: System MUST propagate setting changes to dependent services within 1 minute via polling mechanism
attrs.rationale: Restated by General Module Rule 3 (60-second polling interval), the Entry Points and Main Flow step 15.

nodes.title: Settings cache invalidated immediately on save

attrs.statement: System MUST invalidate settings cache immediately upon save to trigger propagation
attrs.rationale: Restated by General Module Rule 4 and Main Flow step 13.

attrs.statement: System MUST NOT support rollback. Admins make forward-only changes; version history is read-only.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Executive Summary and the Admin Platform scope.

nodes.title: Version history newest first with diff highlighting

attrs.statement: System MUST display version history in reverse chronological order with diff highlighting (old → new)
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Screen 7 business rules.

attrs.statement: System MUST store authentication throttling settings: max login attempts (1-10), lockout duration (5-60 minutes)
attrs.rationale: Restated by Main Flow step 8, Alternative Flow B1 and the Admin Editability Rules; Screen 2 field validation ranges.

attrs.statement: System MUST store OTP configuration: expiry time (5-30 minutes), resend cooldown (30-300 seconds), max resend attempts (3-10)
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Admin Editability Rules and the Screen 3 field validation ranges.

attrs.statement: System MUST store centrally managed country list: country name, ISO code, calling code, country flag asset URL (stored via S-05 Media Storage, nullable), display order, active status
attrs.rationale: Flag assets are stored in centralized media storage/CDN (S-05) and referenced by URL. Screen 4 marks the Country Flag field Required = Yes while this rule and Entity 4 say nullable; see the open question on country flag.

attrs.statement: System MUST store centrally managed discovery question options: answer option, display order, active status

nodes.title: OTP email templates stored with version number

attrs.statement: System MUST store OTP email templates: template name, subject line, HTML body, plain text body, version number

nodes.title: Sensitive values masked in UI and audit logs

attrs.statement: System MUST mask sensitive values (API keys, secrets) in UI and audit logs (display as "••••••••" or "[REDACTED]")
attrs.rationale: Restated by Privacy Rule 1 (UI) and Privacy Rule 2 (audit logs), and the Admin Platform scope.

nodes.title: "View Sensitive Settings" limited to authorized admins

attrs.statement: System MUST restrict "View Sensitive Settings" permission to authorized admins only
attrs.rationale: Restated by Privacy Rule 3 and the Admin Platform scope.

nodes.title: Sensitive values encrypted at rest with AES-256

attrs.statement: System MUST encrypt sensitive values at rest using AES-256

nodes.title: Admin MFA is a future requirement tied to FR-031

attrs.statement: Multi-factor authentication for admin access to Settings Management UI is a future (non-MVP) requirement and MUST be enforced once the shared MFA stack (FR-031) is delivered.
attrs.rationale: Future (non-MVP) requirement; the PRD defers it to the shared MFA stack of FR-031.

nodes.title: Settings API rate limited to 100 requests per minute per admin

attrs.statement: System MUST rate limit Settings API to 100 requests/minute per admin to prevent abuse

nodes.title: Audit logs retained for at least 10 years

attrs.statement: System MUST retain audit logs for minimum 10 years per compliance requirements
attrs.rationale: Restated by Audit Rule 3 and the Security Considerations compliance bullet.

nodes.title: Admin inputs validated against XSS, SQL and command injection

attrs.statement: System MUST validate all admin inputs to prevent XSS, SQL injection, command injection attacks

nodes.title: Settings API exposed for dependent services to poll

attrs.statement: System MUST expose Settings API (RESTful) for dependent services to poll configurations

nodes.title: Settings API response carries version, values and last-modified

attrs.statement: Settings API MUST return JSON response with version number, setting values, and last modified timestamp

nodes.title: Settings API supports OAuth 2.0 with read:settings and write:settings

attrs.statement: Settings API MUST support OAuth 2.0 authentication with "read:settings" or "write:settings" scopes
System MUST NOT expose a rollback API.

nodes.title: Patient configuration response returns treatment areas and lead days together

attrs.statement: The patient configuration response MUST return active ordered treatment-area options and `minimum_inquiry_lead_days` together so the client calendar and backend validator use one configuration source.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5c adds that the API must not return inactive options for new inquiries.

nodes.title: Settings API returns the whole Quote Configuration at once

attrs.statement: The authenticated Settings API MUST return the quote currency, the quote expiry window, both lead times, the slot-hold duration, the configuration version, and the last-modified timestamp together, so FR-004 sends each parent Quote from one consistent configuration version and can record that version on the quote.
attrs.rationale: Quote currency and expiry window are copied onto the quote at first send by FR-004.

nodes.title: Quote Configuration changes affect only quotes first sent after activation

attrs.statement: Quote Configuration changes MUST affect only quotes first sent after activation; the currency and expiry already copied onto a sent quote MUST remain unchanged, drafts MUST carry neither value, and no per-quote extension is allowed.
attrs.rationale: Restated by workflow A7 step 6 and the Screen 5d business rules.

nodes.title: Settings API returns the whole Analytics Configuration at once

attrs.statement: The authenticated Settings API MUST return all Analytics Configuration values with the configuration version and last-modified timestamp so FR-014 calculations use one consistent version and can record it with their aggregates.

nodes.title: Analytics Configuration changes apply to every displayed period; exports untouched

attrs.statement: Analytics Configuration changes MUST apply from FR-014's next calculation or benchmark refresh to every period then displayed (past periods are not frozen), and MUST NOT rewrite exports or scheduled-export files that were already generated.
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Screen 5e recalculation rule.

nodes.title: Each slot hold uses the duration in effect when placed

attrs.statement: Each slot hold MUST use the slot-hold duration in effect when the hold is placed (at subquote acceptance or an FR-006 admin revive); later changes MUST NOT alter an existing hold, and payment failure MUST NOT extend or restart a hold.
attrs.rationale: Restated by workflow A7 step 7, the Screen 5d business rules and the edge case on changing the slot-hold duration while holds are active.

nodes.title: Lead-time changes apply only to reminders not yet sent

attrs.statement: Changes to the quote-expiring-soon or hold-expiring-soon lead time MUST apply only to reminders not yet sent.
System MUST store centrally managed inquiry cancellation reason options: reason label, requires_explanation flag, display order, active status. Consumer: FR-003 Screen 8a.
attrs.rationale: PRD id REQ-026-012a, renumbered. Consumer FR-003 Screen 8a.

attrs.statement: System MUST store centrally managed account deletion reason options: reason label, requires_explanation flag, display order, active status. Consumer: FR-001 Screen 16.
attrs.rationale: PRD id REQ-026-012b, renumbered. Consumer FR-001 Screen 16.

attrs.statement: System MUST store centrally managed inquiry treatment-area options: stable option ID, label, image/icon asset URL, display order, and active status. Consumer: FR-003 Screen 1.
attrs.rationale: PRD id REQ-026-012c, renumbered. Consumer FR-003 Screen 1.

nodes.title: Versioned minimum inquiry lead time, 0 to 730 days

attrs.statement: System MUST store a versioned minimum inquiry lead time as a whole number of days from 0 through 730. Default: 3 days. Consumer: FR-003 Screen 5 and submission validation.
attrs.rationale: PRD id REQ-026-012d, renumbered. Consumer FR-003 Screen 5.

nodes.title: Final active treatment-area option cannot be deactivated

attrs.statement: System MUST prevent deactivation of the final active inquiry treatment-area option.
attrs.rationale: PRD id REQ-026-012e, renumbered.

nodes.title: One versioned Quote Configuration; currency is the FR-029 Default Currency

attrs.statement: System MUST store one versioned Quote Configuration containing the quote expiry window (whole hours from 24 to 336, default 48), the quote-expiring-soon lead time (whole hours from 1 up to half of the expiry window, default 12), the slot-hold duration (whole hours from 24 to 168, default 48), and the hold-expiring-soon lead time (whole hours from 1 up to half of the slot-hold duration, default 12). The quote currency MUST be the FR-029 Default Currency, not a separate setting, and each change to the FR-029 Default Currency MUST create a new Quote Configuration version so the version recorded on a quote identifies both the hours and the currency used. Consumers: FR-004 (currency, expiry window, quote-expiring-soon lead time), FR-005 and FR-006 (slot-hold duration), and FR-006 (hold-expiring-soon lead time).
attrs.rationale: PRD id REQ-026-012f, renumbered. FR-026 keeps no second currency setting.

attrs.statement: System MUST store one versioned Analytics Configuration containing TTFQ SLA target (positive whole minutes, default 120), At Risk threshold (whole days, default 7), Dormant threshold (whole days, greater than At Risk, default 30), price outlier threshold (whole percent 1-100, default 30), benchmark refresh frequency (Daily, Weekly, or Monthly; default Weekly), and optional target monthly commission (blank by default). Consumer: FR-014.
attrs.rationale: PRD id REQ-026-012g, renumbered. Consumer FR-014.

attrs.statement: System MUST store a centrally managed Provider Specialties list: stable specialty ID, specialty name (max 100 chars, unique case-insensitive), display order, active status; seeded with Hair Transplant Surgeon, Dermatologist, Trichologist, Plastic Surgeon, Other. Admins can add, rename, reorder, and deactivate values (no hard delete); at least one value MUST remain active; changes MUST be versioned and audit-logged. Deactivated values MUST be hidden from new selection while providers that hold them keep and still display them; renames MUST apply to display everywhere. Consumer: FR-015 Screen 2 Step 2 and Screen 3 Tab 1.
attrs.rationale: PRD id REQ-026-012h, renumbered. Consumer FR-015.

attrs.statement: Patient Platform (P-01) consumes authentication policies, OTP configurations, country/calling code lists, discovery question options, inquiry cancellation reason options, and account deletion reason options. Provider Platform (PR-06 and PR-02) consumes centrally managed profile lists and the versioned Quote Configuration. Quote Acceptance and Booking (FR-005 and FR-006) consume the versioned slot-hold duration and the hold-expiring-soon reminder lead time. Admin Platform (A-02) FR-015 consumes the Provider Specialties list. Analytics (PR-05 and A-08) FR-014 consumes the versioned Analytics Configuration. Shared Services (S-03) Notification Service consumes OTP email templates. Admin Platform (A-09) is the primary interface for viewing, editing, and versioning all settings.
attrs.rationale: Module Scope, Multi-Tenant Architecture.

nodes.title: Patient platform applies throttling, OTP and centrally managed lists

attrs.statement: Patient registration and login flows apply authentication throttling policies. OTP verification for email confirmation applies OTP expiry and resend cooldown. Profile forms use centrally managed country and calling code lists. Discovery questions ("How did you find us?") display options from the centralized list.
attrs.rationale: Module Scope, Multi-Tenant Breakdown, Patient Platform (P-01).

nodes.title: Provider platform applies throttling and OTP parameters

attrs.statement: Authentication throttling (PR-01) applies to provider login attempts. OTP parameters (PR-01) apply to provider email verification flows. Provider staff management (PR-06) indirectly uses centrally managed lists.
attrs.rationale: Module Scope, Multi-Tenant Breakdown, Provider Platform.

attrs.statement: Out of scope for FR-026: actual email sending (handled by S-03: Notification Service); SMS notifications (future enhancement, V2); push notification templates (handled separately in notification preferences module); legal content management (see FR-027: Terms & Conditions, Privacy Policy, Consent forms); regional configuration and pricing (see FR-028: Location presentation, starting prices by currency); payment system configuration (see FR-029: Stripe account management, conversion rates, split payment rules); notification rules and event-based triggers (see FR-030: Event-to-notification mapping, channel configuration); admin access control and role-based permissions (see FR-031: Role management, permission matrix).
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure, Out of Scope. Boundary recorded as the PRD states it (D10).

attrs.statement: Admin reaches settings through Settings, Authentication & Security (throttling policies), Settings, App Data (country lists, discovery questions, inquiry cancellation reasons, account deletion reasons, provider specialties, inquiry configuration, quote configuration), Settings, Notifications (OTP email templates) and Settings, Analytics (analytics configuration consumed by FR-014).
attrs.rationale: Entry Points, Admin-Initiated.

nodes.title: Out-of-range values rejected before save with a range message

attrs.statement: The system validates admin input before save and rejects an out-of-range value with an error message stating the valid range (for example, "Max Login Attempts must be between 1 and 10" for 0); the admin corrects the value and the system re-validates.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B1.

nodes.title: Consumers keep cached settings when the Settings API fails

attrs.statement: If a consuming platform cannot retrieve updated settings (for example a network timeout on the Settings API), it logs the error, continues using its cached settings, and retries on the next scheduled 60-second poll; on a successful retry it applies the updated settings. The system logs the propagation delay but does not alert (self-healing).
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B2, the Settings API unreachable edge case and Integration 1. The edge case and Integration 1 say cached settings are used for up to 1 minute, then the error is logged and the poll retried; see the open question on cache duration.

nodes.title: Notification Service falls back to a default template

attrs.statement: If the Settings API is unreachable when the Notification Service retrieves an OTP email template, the Notification Service uses a fallback template (hardcoded default) and logs the error for admin review.
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Integration 2 (a business rule inside the technical section).

nodes.title: Settings API stays available during deployments

attrs.statement: The Settings API remains available during deployments; the Patient app retrieves settings after restart; no data is lost.
attrs.rationale: Edge case on settings propagation during a Patient app deployment.

nodes.title: Concurrent edits to one setting group are detected before save

attrs.statement: The system detects a concurrent edit by two admins to the same setting group before save and displays a modal popup: "This setting was updated by [admin email] 30 seconds ago. Your changes may conflict. Review the latest version before saving." The modal shows a diff of the latest changes and the options "Reload Latest Version" or "Save Anyway (Overwrite)".
attrs.rationale: Edge case on concurrent edits.

nodes.title: Timestamps stored in UTC, shown in the admin local timezone

attrs.statement: All timestamps MUST be stored in UTC and displayed in admin's local timezone.
attrs.rationale: General Module Rule 5.

nodes.title: Admin activity logs exempt from GDPR deletion requests

attrs.statement: Admin activity logs are exempt from GDPR deletion requests (business records, legal requirement).
attrs.rationale: Data & Privacy Rules, GDPR line.

nodes.title: Sensitive values masked in version history; unmask by permission

attrs.statement: Sensitive values are masked in version history (displayed as "[REDACTED]"); admins with "View Sensitive Settings" permission can click "Show" to unmask them.
attrs.rationale: Edge case on sensitive value visibility in version history, and the Screen 7 business rule.

nodes.title: Audit trail also records IP address and user agent

attrs.statement: All admin actions are logged with IP address, user agent, timestamp, and change details.
attrs.rationale: Security Considerations, Audit trail. REQ-026-004 lists a narrower set of audit fields; the lists are complementary.

nodes.title: Settings roles and what each may do

attrs.statement: Role-based access control is enforced: the "Settings Manager" role can view and edit all settings; the "Settings Viewer" role can view settings and version history (read-only); the "Security Admin" role can view sensitive values (API keys, secrets) unmasked.
attrs.rationale: Security Considerations and Dependencies. FR-031 owns role management and the permission matrix; this rule records only what FR-026 states. See the open question on roles versus the "Settings Management" permission.

attrs.statement: Password policy is fixed in codebase and not admin-editable: minimum 12 characters, at least 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 digit, 1 special character from !@#$%^&(),.?":{}|<>.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules, Fixed in Codebase; shown view-only on Screen 1.

nodes.title: IP and device rate limiting fixed, independent of per-user throttling

attrs.statement: IP/device-level rate limiting is fixed at the application layer and not admin-configurable: max 20 failed login attempts per IP address per hour with a 1-hour IP lockout. It is enforced independently of the per-user authentication throttling configured in Screen 2; both constraints apply simultaneously (whichever triggers first locks the user out).
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules, Fixed in Codebase, and Security Considerations.

attrs.statement: The discovery question text is FIXED as "How did you find out about us?" and is not editable.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules, Fixed in Codebase, and Screen 5.

attrs.statement: OTP email template names are fixed: admins cannot rename the templates.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules, Fixed in Codebase, and Screen 6.

attrs.statement: The setting group structure is predefined: admins cannot create new setting groups.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules, Fixed in Codebase.

nodes.title: OTP code length fixed at 6 digits

attrs.statement: OTP code length is FIXED at 6 digits in codebase and is not editable.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability Rules, Fixed in Codebase, and Screen 3 business rules.

nodes.title: FR-024 and FR-011 build on the FR-026 settings infrastructure

attrs.statement: FR-026 provides the settings infrastructure (audit trail, versioning, UI shell); FR-024 implements treatment-specific CRUD operations and FR-011 implements aftercare milestone template management within that infrastructure, sharing the Settings Management UI and audit trail.
attrs.rationale: Dependencies, Downstream Consumers. Listed for traceability.

nodes.title: A reason deactivated mid-flow is still accepted for that submission

attrs.statement: If an admin deactivates a cancellation reason while a patient is mid-cancellation, the patient app uses its cached reason list (up to 1 minute stale); a submission with a now-deactivated reason is still accepted because the reason was valid at flow start, and the next cancellation flow loads the updated list.
attrs.rationale: Edge case on deactivating a cancellation reason mid-flow.

nodes.title: Quote send blocked when the Settings API is unavailable

attrs.statement: If the Settings API is unavailable as a provider first sends a quote, FR-004 blocks the send and keeps the quote as a draft; the quote is never sent with a guessed or stale currency or expiry. The provider can retry.
attrs.rationale: Edge case on the Settings API being unavailable at first send.

attrs.statement: Discovery Questions are seeded with "Search Engine" (Order 1), "Social Media" (Order 2) and "Friend Referral" (Order 3).
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Initial Configuration / Seeding.

attrs.statement: Inquiry Cancellation Reasons are seeded with: "Changed my mind" (Order 1), "Found a better option elsewhere" (2), "Medical concerns" (3), "Financial reasons" (4), "Travel restrictions" (5), "Timeline doesn't work" (6), each with Requires Explanation = No; and "Other" (7) with Requires Explanation = Yes, FIXED, which cannot be deactivated.
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Initial Configuration / Seeding.

attrs.statement: Account Deletion Reasons are seeded with: "I no longer use this app" (Order 1), "I found a better alternative" (2), "The app doesn't meet my needs" (3), "Too many notifications or emails" (4), "Concerns about privacy or data security" (5), "I had technical issues or bugs" (6), "The app is difficult to use" (7), "I'm taking a break and may return later" (8), each with Requires Explanation = No; and "Others" (9) with Requires Explanation = Yes, FIXED, which cannot be deactivated.
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Initial Configuration / Seeding.

attrs.statement: The country list is seeded with at least: Turkey (TR, +90), UK (GB, +44), USA (US, +1) and Germany (DE, +49).
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Initial Configuration / Seeding (minimum initial set).

attrs.statement: The default "Verification Email" and "Password Reset Email" templates MUST be seeded with standard branding and variables.
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Initial Configuration / Seeding.

nodes.title: Template HTML sanitized; previews run under a restrictive policy

attrs.statement: Email template HTML MUST be sanitized server-side: script, iframe, form and similar tags, event-handler attributes, and javascript:, data: and other non-whitelisted URL protocols (only http, https and mailto are allowed) are stripped or rejected, and dangerous CSS is removed; variable substitution still renders. The template preview MUST render with a restrictive content security policy that blocks scripts.
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Security Considerations, HTML Sanitization for Email Templates (a business rule inside the technical section). Condensed: tag and attribute allow-lists, library names and XSS test cases stay in the technical spec.

nodes.title: Throttling changes apply immediately, with no staging

attrs.statement: Authentication throttling changes apply immediately upon save (no staging); new login attempts apply the new throttling policy immediately after propagation.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 business rules, restated by Main Flow step 16.

nodes.title: Existing lockouts keep their original duration

attrs.statement: Existing locked-out users continue to serve their existing lockout duration (no retroactive changes); security policy changes apply prospectively only.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 business rules and the business process assumption that security policy changes apply prospectively only.

nodes.title: One OTP expiry for verification and password reset

attrs.statement: Single global OTP expiry: the configured OTP Expiry Time applies uniformly to both email verification and password reset OTP flows (no separate per-flow expiry).
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 business rules and field description.

nodes.title: OTP changes apply only to new OTP requests

attrs.statement: OTP configuration changes apply only to NEW OTP generation requests; existing OTP codes in users' inboxes retain their original expiry time.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 business rules.

nodes.title: OTP resend needs cooldown elapsed and hourly limit not exceeded

attrs.statement: The system enforces BOTH resend constraints simultaneously (whichever is more restrictive applies): the user must wait at least Resend Cooldown seconds between consecutive resend requests, and cannot exceed Max Resend Attempts resend requests within a 1-hour window. A user can resend an OTP if and only if the cooldown has elapsed since the last resend AND the hourly limit is not exceeded.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3, Rate Limiting Interaction Logic. The worked scenarios are examples; see the open question on scenario 3.

nodes.title: Hourly OTP resend counter uses a rolling 60-minute window

attrs.statement: The hourly resend counter is the number of resend requests in the last 60 minutes from the current time (rolling window), not a counter that resets at fixed hourly boundaries, to prevent burst abuse.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3, Counter Reset Logic. The PRD labels the rolling window "RECOMMENDED" and then states "Implementation: Use rolling window to prevent burst abuse"; read as the rule.

nodes.title: Country names and ISO codes must be unique and valid

attrs.statement: Country names must be unique (max 100 characters). ISO codes must be unique, exactly 2 uppercase characters, and valid per the ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 standard.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 business rules and field validation. Workflow A1 step 7 says the system "validates country code uniqueness" without saying which code; see the open question.

nodes.title: Calling codes may be shared by countries

attrs.statement: Calling codes can be duplicated (for example USA and Canada both use +1); the format is +[1-4 digits].
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 business rules and field validation.

attrs.statement: Deactivating a country does NOT delete it (soft delete, archived); a country cannot be hard-deleted; patients who selected a deactivated country retain their selection and the country is hidden from new users.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 business rules and the edge case on deleting a country that active patients have selected.

attrs.statement: SVG is the preferred format for country flags; PNG is allowed only when SVG is not available. PNG uploads must be at least 128x128 with a square (1:1) aspect ratio; the maximum file size is 1 MB.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 business rules and the Country Flag field validation.

nodes.title: Discovery answer options must be unique

attrs.statement: Discovery answer options must be unique (max 100 characters).
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 business rules and field validation.

nodes.title: At least 2 discovery options stay active

attrs.statement: At least 2 active discovery question options must exist at all times; deactivating one of the last 2 active options is prevented.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 business rules and the matching edge case error "At least 2 active options required. Cannot deactivate this option."

nodes.title: Deactivating a discovery option keeps historical data

attrs.statement: Deactivating a discovery question option does NOT delete historical data.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 business rules.

attrs.statement: Inquiry cancellation reason labels must be unique (case-insensitive; max 100 characters).
attrs.rationale: Screen 5a business rules and field validation.

nodes.title: At least 2 cancellation reasons stay active

attrs.statement: At least 2 active inquiry cancellation reasons must exist at all times.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5a business rules.

nodes.title: "Other" cancellation reason is fixed and needs an explanation

attrs.statement: The "Other" cancellation reason is FIXED (cannot be deactivated or deleted) and always requires an explanation.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5a business rules and the matching edge case error.

nodes.title: Deactivating a cancellation reason keeps history

attrs.statement: Deactivating a cancellation reason does NOT delete historical data; previously captured cancellation reasons retain their original label in audit logs.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5a business rules.

nodes.title: Requires Explanation shows a mandatory free text field in FR-003

attrs.statement: When Requires Explanation is true for a cancellation reason, FR-003 Screen 8a must show a mandatory free text field (max 500 characters) when that reason is selected.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5a business rules. Consumer FR-003 Screen 8a reads this list to populate the cancellation reason selector.

attrs.statement: Account deletion reason labels must be unique (case-insensitive; max 100 characters).
attrs.rationale: Screen 5b business rules and field validation.

nodes.title: At least 2 deletion reasons stay active

attrs.statement: At least 2 active account deletion reasons must exist at all times.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5b business rules.

nodes.title: "Others" deletion reason is fixed and needs an explanation

attrs.statement: The "Others" deletion reason is FIXED (cannot be deactivated or deleted) and always requires an explanation.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5b business rules and the matching edge case error.

nodes.title: Deactivating a deletion reason keeps history

attrs.statement: Deactivating an account deletion reason does NOT delete historical data; previously captured deletion reasons retain their original label in audit logs.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5b business rules.

nodes.title: Requires Explanation shows an optional free text field in FR-001

attrs.statement: When Requires Explanation is true for a deletion reason, FR-001 Screen 16 must show an optional free text field (max 500 characters) when that reason is selected (the deletion reason field overall remains optional per FR-001 business rules).
attrs.rationale: Screen 5b business rules. The field description and workflow A5 step 4 say the patient "must provide free text"; this rule follows the Screen 5b business rule line. See the open question on mandatory versus optional.

nodes.title: Treatment-area options: admin operations and deletion limit

attrs.statement: Admin may create, edit, reorder, activate, or deactivate treatment-area options. Options referenced by an inquiry cannot be deleted.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5c business rules and workflow A6.

nodes.title: Inactive options hidden from new inquiries; history keeps the snapshot

attrs.statement: The patient configuration API must not return inactive treatment-area options for new inquiries. Historical inquiry views use the saved option snapshot, and submitted inquiries retain their historical treatment-area snapshot.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5c business rules and workflow A6 step 7.

nodes.title: Lead time applies to the calendar and to submission validation

attrs.statement: Minimum Inquiry Lead Time applies to both the calendar's disabled-date calculation and backend inquiry submission validation.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5c business rules.

attrs.statement: On save, the system validates that active treatment-area option labels are unique (max 100 characters), that an image/icon asset is present and resolves to an approved S-05-managed asset, that display order is a unique integer, and that the lead time is between 0 and 730 days.
attrs.rationale: Workflow A6 step 5 and Screen 5c field validation.

nodes.title: Conversion and exchange-rate locking stay with FR-029

attrs.statement: Currency conversion and exchange-rate locking remain owned by FR-029 and occur at acceptance; the Quote Configuration screen does not manage conversion rates.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5d business rules. Boundary recorded as the PRD states it (D10).

nodes.title: Blank monthly commission goal hides the FR-014 reference line

attrs.statement: When Target Monthly Commission is blank, FR-014 hides the reference line; clearing a previously set value hides it again.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5e business rules.

attrs.statement: Per-provider SLA overrides are out of scope; all providers are measured against the same platform SLA target.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5e business rules.

attrs.statement: The system validates analytics configuration values (for example, Dormant must be greater than At Risk) and blocks save on error.
attrs.rationale: Workflow A8 step 3 and the Screen 5e field validation.

nodes.title: Template subject and body must include {code}

attrs.statement: The subject and body of an OTP email template must include the {code} variable; the system warns if {code} is missing.
attrs.rationale: Screen 6 business rules and Admin Editability Rules.

nodes.title: Template HTML body validated on save

attrs.statement: The HTML body of an OTP email template must be valid HTML; the system validates it on save.
attrs.rationale: Screen 6 business rules.

nodes.title: Plain text body is the fallback version

attrs.statement: The plain text body is the fallback for email clients that do not support HTML.
attrs.rationale: Screen 6 business rules.

nodes.title: Template variables substituted at send time

attrs.statement: Template variables ({code}, {email}, {expiry_minutes}, {app_name}) are automatically substituted at send time.
attrs.rationale: Screen 6 business rules and Available Variables field. Communication Structure lists only {code}, {email} and {expiry_minutes}; this rule follows the Screen 6 list. See the open question on {app_name}.

nodes.title: Template preview uses fake sample data

attrs.statement: Template preview renders a sample email with fake data (for example {code} = "123456", {expiry_minutes} = "15").
attrs.rationale: Screen 6 business rules, Notes and workflow A2 step 6.

nodes.title: Template changes apply only to new OTP requests

attrs.statement: Template changes apply only to NEW OTP generation requests; users already in a verification flow continue with the previous template version and existing emails are unchanged.
attrs.rationale: Screen 6 business rules, Module Scope (Shared Services S-03) and workflow A2 steps 11 and 12.

nodes.title: Dashboard access needs the "Settings Management" permission

attrs.statement: Only admins with "Settings Management" permission can access the Settings Management Dashboard.
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 business rules. REQ-026-001 names the roles "Settings Manager" and "Settings Viewer" instead; see the open question on permission naming.

nodes.title: Setting groups organized into four sections

attrs.statement: Setting groups are organized into sections: Authentication & Security (Authentication Throttling, OTP Configuration, Password Policy), App Data (Countries & Calling Codes, Discovery Questions, Inquiry Cancellation Reasons, Account Deletion Reasons, Provider Specialties, Inquiry Configuration, Quote Configuration), Notifications (OTP Email Templates: Verification Email, Password Reset Email), and Analytics (Analytics Configuration).
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 business rules and Setting Groups (detailed). Code length is fixed and view-only; Password Policy is fixed in codebase and view-only.

nodes.title: Edit disabled for groups fixed in codebase

attrs.statement: The "Edit" button is disabled for setting groups marked as "Fixed in Codebase".
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 business rules.

attrs.statement: "View History" is always available (read-only).
attrs.rationale: Screen 1 business rules.

nodes.title: Lists show how many users picked each value

attrs.statement: The list managers show usage counts: how many patients selected each discovery option (and each cancellation and deletion reason, with a date range filter) and how many users selected each country, how many providers hold each specialty, with a warning before deactivating a frequently selected or held value.
attrs.rationale: Notes on Screens 4, 5, 5a, 5b and 5f. The usage_count fields on the option and reason entities are calculated by this rule.

nodes.title: Admins create, edit, preview and publish legal documents

attrs.statement: Admins MUST be able to create, edit, preview, and publish legal documents (T&C, Privacy, Consent, Cancellation Policy)
attrs.rationale: Restated by Main Flow step 1 and 2 (lines 85-86), Screens 1 to 3, Admin Platform scope (lines 25, 43) and the assumption that Admins manage all legal content centrally within A-09 settings (line 396). Document types are the four of Key Entities (line 358).

nodes.title: Version history kept with timestamps and change tracking

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain version history with timestamps and change tracking; previous versions are preserved for reference
attrs.rationale: Restated by Admin Platform scope (line 44: maintain version history and compare versions, diff summary) and Shared Services (line 50: version registry for type, locale, version, status; Executive Summary line 13: preserving full version history).

nodes.title: Effective date scheduling; publication is global

attrs.statement: Admins MUST be able to schedule an effective date for publication; publication applies globally (no regional variants)
attrs.rationale: Restated by Main Flow step 3 (line 87), Screen 1 business rule (line 148: publish is global, no region targeting, locale is for translation display only), Screen 3 business rule (line 206: publication is global, no regional or locale targeting) and CL-4 (line 352: legal content is uniform globally, no location-based variants or region-specific publication paths).

nodes.title: Acceptance required for material changes as configured

attrs.statement: System MUST require acceptance for material changes as configured, prompting users appropriately
attrs.rationale: Restated by Main Flow step 6 (line 90: acceptance prompts triggered from the configured scope), Screen 2 business rule (line 177: Material Change=true triggers the acceptance requirement after publish) and Screen 3 business rule (line 205: publishing triggers acceptance prompts if Material Change=true). What is configurable is not specified (open question).

nodes.title: Acceptance tracked per user, document type and version

attrs.statement: System MUST track which user accepted which document type and version, with timestamp and locale displayed
attrs.rationale: Restated by Patient Platform scope (lines 23, 33: acceptance recorded with timestamp and version ID), Shared Services (line 51: acceptance ledger per user, per document type and version) and Main Flow step 3 of User Accepts New Version (line 102).

nodes.title: Admin view of acceptance status and follow-up needs

attrs.statement: System MUST provide a coverage view for Admin to see acceptance status and follow‑up needs
attrs.rationale: Restated by Admin Platform scope (line 46: monitor acceptance status and outstanding users), Screens 4 and 4A, and User Story 3 (lines 299-307).

attrs.statement: All legal content changes MUST be logged with who/when/what changed (audit trail)
attrs.rationale: Restated by Main Flow step 5 (line 89), Shared Services (line 52: audit trail for all create/edit/publish actions), Screen 3 business rule (line 205: publishing logs an audit entry) and User Story 1 scenario 2.
