At most one Stripe account can be marked as Global Fallback; Global Fallback cannot have explicit country/regional grouping assignments
attrs.rationale: Restated by the Global Fallback field validation (Screen 1). Payment Rule 2 adds that without an assigned account or fallback the payment is blocked (see the unsupported-location rule).

nodes.title: Assigned countries are groups or countries, not both

attrs.statement: | Assigned Countries | multi-select | Conditional | Countries or regional groupings served by this account (mutually exclusive per record: choose groups or countries, not both) | Required unless Global Fallback is enabled. Each country/grouping can map to only one Stripe account (overrides required to reassign). If a country mapping exists, it overrides any group-level account for that country. |
attrs.rationale: Taken from the Assigned Countries field description (Screen 1).

nodes.title: Supported currencies compatible with assigned countries

attrs.statement: Supported currencies must be compatible with assigned countries (e.g., EUR for European countries)

nodes.title: Stripe connection can be tested at any time

attrs.statement: Admin can test Stripe connection at any time by clicking "Test Connection" button Show warning icon if Stripe account hasn't been tested in over 30 days Logs test attempt (admin, timestamp, result) and updates "Last Tested" timestamp/status badge

nodes.title: Unsupported location blocks payment and alerts admin

attrs.statement: If no fallback: System displays error to patient: "Payment processing not available for your location. Please contact support." System sends alert to admin: "Payment attempted from unsupported country: South Africa. Configure Stripe account for this region."
attrs.rationale: Edge case (PRD line 1134) adds that the payment attempt is logged to the admin dashboard for follow-up. B6 line 378: when the Global Fallback is used, a warning is logged to the admin.

attrs.statement: How to manage admin accidentally entering incorrect Stripe secret key that initially validates but later fails during actual payment processing? During configuration, system validates Stripe credentials by making test API call to Stripe. If credentials are syntactically correct but have insufficient permissions or are later revoked by Stripe, first payment attempt will fail. Payment Processing Service logs error: "Stripe authentication failed for account [name]." System sends urgent alert to admin: "Stripe account [name] failed authentication. Verify API keys are active and have required permissions." System temporarily routes payments to Global Fallback (if configured) and displays error banner to admin.
attrs.rationale: PRD line 1142: payments are temporarily routed to the Global Fallback when configured.

attrs.statement: Failure handling: If Stripe API unavailable, queue payment transactions for retry with exponential backoff, notify admin of Stripe outage
Secret rotation: Support for Stripe API key rotation without downtime (configure new keys, test, then deactivate old keys)
attrs.rationale: PRD Implementation Notes: configure new keys, test, then deactivate old keys.

nodes.title: Editing a rate source re-runs the connection test

attrs.statement: Edit Source: Admin can update source name, API key. System re-runs test connection on save.

nodes.title: Rate source connection can be tested at any time

attrs.statement: Test Connection: Available per source at any time. Calls the provider API, updates Status and Last Tested.

nodes.title: Rate source credentials encrypted and masked

attrs.statement: API credentials are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and never logged in plain text (mask all but last 4 characters)
attrs.rationale: Restates REQ-029-028 and REQ-029-029 for rate source credentials.

nodes.title: Rate source health checked during syncs

attrs.statement: System periodically checks source health during scheduled syncs and updates the Status indicator. If a source becomes unhealthy, all pairs using that source display a visual warning badge (yellow/red) on the pair list.
attrs.rationale: The Status field of the rate source is calculated by this rule.

nodes.title: Rate protection does not stop payments

attrs.statement: Rate protection alerts do not automatically stop payments; they surface visual cues and send admin notifications
attrs.rationale: Rate protection is always active for auto-fetch pairs (PRD line 779) and each pair is monitored independently (REQ-029-010).

attrs.statement: Currency pairs must reference currencies that are enabled in the Currency Management screen (Screen 6)
Cannot create a duplicate pair (one pair per target currency; USD/EUR can only exist once)

nodes.title: Pairs always use USD as base

attrs.statement: All pairs MUST use USD as the base currency. Admin selects only the target currency when adding a pair.

nodes.title: Pair deletion warns and falls back to USD

attrs.statement: Delete Pair: Remove a currency pair. System warns: "Deleting this pair means payments involving {Target} currency will fall back to USD. Continue?" Requires confirmation.
attrs.rationale: Deleted or unconfigured target currencies collect payment in USD (REQ-029-011b).

attrs.statement: Status badges update automatically: green when last fetch succeeded and rate change is within threshold; yellow when rate protection threshold was breached in last 7 days or source is degraded; red when last fetch failed or source is down.
attrs.rationale: Status of a pair is calculated by this rule. See the product owner decision on badge reset.

nodes.title: Each pair tracks its own status

attrs.statement: Each pair independently tracks its own status. A source failure affects only pairs using that source; manual pairs are unaffected.

nodes.title: Sync Now fetches a rate immediately

attrs.statement: Sync Now (per pair): For auto-fetched pairs, triggers an immediate rate fetch outside the scheduled sync

nodes.title: Pair switches to manual when its source is deleted

attrs.statement: If the source assigned to this pair is later deleted, the pair gracefully switches to manual mode with the last fetched rate pre-filled as the manual base rate. Admin is notified of this change.
attrs.rationale: Conflicts with the delete-blocked reading (see the product owner decision on rate source deletion).

nodes.title: Deleting a referenced rate source is blocked

attrs.statement: Deleting a source that is referenced by existing pairs is blocked; admin must reassign or convert affected pairs to manual mode first. This is the graceful deletion pattern.
attrs.rationale: Also stated by the Delete Source action (Screen 2A) which requires reassigning or switching the pairs to manual before deletion.

nodes.title: Manual mode pairs have no sync schedule

attrs.statement: Admin enters the base rate directly in the Manual Base Rate field No sync schedule is created; rate only changes when admin manually edits and saves

nodes.title: Switching a pair between auto-fetch and manual

attrs.statement: Auto → Manual: System pre-fills Manual Base Rate with the last fetched rate so admin doesn't start from zero. Sync schedule is removed. Manual → Auto: System requires admin to select a source and run "Test Connection & Fetch Rate" before saving. The fetched rate replaces the manual rate.
The Effective Rate preview updates in real-time as admin changes Base Rate or Markup %, giving immediate visibility into the patient-facing rate.

nodes.title: Failed sync retries with backoff and alerts

attrs.statement: System retries sync after exponential backoff (e.g., retry in 15 minutes, then 30 minutes, then 1 hour)
attrs.rationale: Part of the failed-sync alternative flow (B2). The source status also turns red when the source stays down.

attrs.statement: System detects the USD/EUR rate changed by 4.5% in the last 24 hours (exceeds the 3% global threshold) Admin decides to increase the per-pair markup from 5% to 7% to protect against the unfavorable rate
attrs.rationale: Breach alternative flow (B5): yellow status, urgent alert, admin reviews and adjusts the per-pair markup.

nodes.title: One rate alert per pair per six hours

attrs.statement: How does system handle rapid currency fluctuation exceeding rate protection threshold multiple times in single day for one pair (e.g., USD/EUR changes 3% at 8am, another 3% at 2pm, another 3% at 8pm)? System sends first alert at 8am when the pair's initial 3% threshold is crossed and marks the pair's status as yellow/warning on the pair list. System applies rate-limiting to alerts (maximum one alert per currency pair per 6 hours) to prevent alert fatigue. System accumulates rate changes and sends second alert at 2pm showing cumulative change: "USD/EUR increased 6% in 6 hours." The pair's yellow/warning status persists on Screen 2A until the admin reviews and acknowledges. Admin receives summary of all rate changes across all pairs in daily digest email.

How does system handle a rate source being completely unavailable for 24+ hours? For each auto-fetch pair using the affected source: system continues using the pair's last successfully cached rate, marks the pair's status as red/error on the pair list (Screen 2A), and marks the source's status as red in the Sources section. System sends daily email digest to admin summarizing the source outage and listing all affected pairs. When the source recovers, the next scheduled sync for each affected pair fetches the latest rate and restores green status. Admin can also switch affected pairs to a different source or manual mode at any time during the outage.
When editing an existing pair, show a "Rate History" link/section displaying rate changes over the last 30 days (chart + table)

Booking Total Rule: Throughout this FR, "booking total" means the accepted subquote price after any promotion, in the quote currency, read from the FR-005 acceptance snapshot. The same rule applies to every discount type, including discounts funded only by Hairline: commission is always calculated on the price after promotion. It is never recomputed from the live quote, option, or date-range price. This single figure is the base for the Percentage commission, the deposit amount, and the installment split; any display or charge in another currency uses the rate locked under Currency Rule 2.
attrs.rationale: Same rule applies to every discount type, including discounts funded only by Hairline (see REQ-029-054).

nodes.title: Configuration locks only at named lock points

attrs.statement: Rule 1: Payment configuration changes never alter a value that has already been locked. Each configuration is locked at a named point: (a) the currency conversion rate (including markup) is locked when the patient accepts a subquote in FR-005 and is stored in the acceptance snapshot; (b) the effective commission configuration, the deposit rate, and the split payment (installment) settings are locked at FR-006 booking confirmation and stored with the booking; (c) no payment configuration is frozen when a parent quote or subquote is created or sent in FR-004. Before its lock point, a quote or accepted-but-unconfirmed subquote follows the configuration that is effective at that moment, and an active installment plan keeps the settings locked at its booking confirmation. When FR-019 expresses a fixed-amount promotion in the quote currency at quote send, it uses the currency conversion rate (including markup) in effect at send; this sets the promotion amount on the quote only and does not lock the conversion rate for payment, which stays locked at acceptance under (a).
attrs.rationale: Restated by REQ-029-049 (near duplicate). The lock point for the commission is booking confirmation in FR-006.

nodes.title: Use last known good configuration when unavailable

attrs.statement: Rule 4: System must gracefully handle payment processing when configuration data is unavailable (use last known good configuration)
Payment Rule 3: Currency conversion markup applies to all transactions involving currency conversion (protects against bank rate differences)

nodes.title: Prices shown in the patient's selected currency

attrs.statement: Currency Rule 1: Prices always displayed to patients in their selected currency using admin-configured conversion rates with markup
attrs.rationale: Display in the selected currency uses the admin-configured conversion rates with markup.

attrs.statement: Payment Rule 6: If patient misses installment payment deadline, system sends reminder notification during grace period, then cancels booking if not paid

What happens when patient books procedure 35 days before procedure date with 30-day cutoff enabled, and selects 3 installments? System calculates time between booking date (35 days before) and cutoff date (30 days before) = 5 days available for installments. System determines 3 installments not feasible (would require payments every 1.67 days). System displays error: "Insufficient time for 3 installments. Please select 2 installments or pay in full." Patient must select fewer installments or pay deposit + remaining balance immediately.
attrs.rationale: PRD line 1136: the patient must select fewer installments or pay deposit plus the remaining balance immediately.

nodes.title: Tiered installment plans by booking amount

attrs.statement: Admin creates multiple split payment rule tiers based on booking amount ranges
attrs.rationale: Alternative flow A4. Conflicts with the single global split configuration of Screen 4 (see the product owner decision on tiered installments). The graph models the single configuration.

attrs.statement: System enforces a minimum 30-day cutoff before procedure date (per system booking/payment rules); admins may increase the cutoff up to 90 days

nodes.title: Fewer installments offered when time is short

attrs.statement: If time between booking and procedure is insufficient for selected installments given cutoff, system offers fewer installments

nodes.title: Deposit refunds follow provider cancellation policies

attrs.statement: Refund Rule: Deposit refunds follow provider-specific cancellation policies (separate from payment configuration)
attrs.rationale: Refund handling sits outside payment configuration.

attrs.statement: Payout Rule 1: Payout buffer window determines when payout statements are auto-generated before a scheduled payout date. The buffer window is a global setting (default: 3 days, range: 1–7 days). FR-017 / A-05 reads this value to schedule statement creation for provider and affiliate payouts.
attrs.rationale: Consumed by FR-017 (A-05) to schedule statement creation.

attrs.statement: Deposit rate allowed range (20-30% hard-coded business rule) Split payment installment range (2-9 installments hard-coded limit) Cutoff days allowed range (30-90 days hard-coded limits) Installment frequency (monthly; 30-day intervals) Payment audit logging requirements (always enabled, cannot be disabled)
attrs.rationale: Fixed values, not admin-editable (PRD Admin Editability Rules).

attrs.statement: Provider-specific commission scopes take precedence over the global default at booking confirmation

nodes.title: Commission scope covers one or more providers and can be archived

attrs.statement: A provider-specific commission scope may cover one or multiple providers and may be archived when no longer needed

nodes.title: Single-provider commission edit from FR-015 splits the scope

attrs.statement: Single-provider edit from FR-015: When an admin edits commission in FR-015 Tab 7 for a provider covered by a scope shared with other providers, the system removes that provider from the shared scope and creates a single-provider scope for it with the new values; the shared scope and its other providers are unchanged. The split is audit-logged with before/after state.

nodes.title: One pending future-dated commission configuration per provider

attrs.statement: Scheduled configuration: Each provider has at most one pending future-dated configuration. Saving another future-dated configuration for the same provider replaces the pending one (logged); on its Effective Date the pending configuration becomes the active one automatically. Screen 5 and FR-015 Tab 7 show the same pending configuration, which FR-032 Screen 4 displays read-only to the provider.
attrs.rationale: Same statement as REQ-029-048 second half (near duplicate).

nodes.title: Provider eligibility for a commission scope

attrs.statement: System validates selected providers have status Active or Suspended (Deactivated providers cannot be selected; their existing scopes are read-only) and the commission value matches the selected model: Percentage 0-100% (0.1% precision); Flat Rate amount > 0 in an enabled currency

Percentage model (global default or provider scope): commission amount = booking total (the accepted subquote price after promotion, in the quote currency, from the acceptance snapshot) × snapshotted commission percentage (rounded to 2 decimal places; last payment absorbs rounding difference if needed)
attrs.rationale: Part of the commission calculation; see REQ-029-050 for the booking total.

attrs.statement: Flat Rate model (provider scope only): commission amount = the snapshotted fixed amount, deducted once per completed procedure (FR-010 completion milestone), regardless of procedure price; it is not charged per package, per Subquote, or per installment

nodes.title: Flat Rate amount kept in its configured currency

attrs.statement: Flat Rate amounts are stored and snapshotted in their configured currency; this screen introduces no new currency conversion rule, and any conversion follows the existing FR-029 currency configuration and downstream FR-017 reconciliation handling
The global default is percentage-only; the Flat Rate model is available for provider-specific scopes only
attrs.rationale: Restated by REQ-029-043.

attrs.statement: Currency codes are immutable and come from a system-maintained catalog; admins cannot add non-ISO or custom codes.

nodes.title: One default currency and at least one enabled

attrs.statement: At least one currency must remain enabled at all times. Exactly one enabled currency must be set as the system default.

nodes.title: Disabling a referenced currency warns with a resolution path

attrs.statement: If an admin attempts to disable a currency currently referenced by system configuration (e.g., used in Stripe account supported currencies, location starting prices, or active pricing configs), the system MUST warn and provide a safe resolution path (e.g., update dependent configs first) before allowing the disable.
attrs.rationale: Overlaps REQ-029-052 (blocked while in use). See the product owner decision on warn versus block.

nodes.title: Currency enable and disable affects new choices only

attrs.statement: Enabling/disabling currencies affects new configuration choices immediately; existing records retain their stored currency codes.

nodes.title: Currency management is the source of truth for dropdowns

attrs.statement: This screen is the source of truth for currency dropdowns across Admin/Provider/Patient experiences (where applicable). FR-017 Screen 1 ("Financial Reporting - Revenue Dashboard") initializes its reporting currency selector from this system default currency; the MVP seed value is USD unless an admin changes it later.
Concurrency: Payment configuration updates must use optimistic locking to prevent race conditions when multiple admins edit simultaneously
Failure handling: If email service unavailable, log notification failures and display in-app notification to admin, retry with queue

What occurs if admin configures cutoff date (e.g., 60 days) that prevents any installment options from being offered for most bookings? attrs.rationale: Overlaps REQ-029-042. The admin may proceed and a warning is logged to the admin activity log.

nodes.title: Revived booking resolves commission, deposit and split settings at the later confirmation

nodes.title: Admins create notification rules per event

attrs.statement: System MUST allow admins to create notification rules by selecting event type, configuring recipient targeting, enabling delivery channels (email, push, and SMS in future phases), selecting templates per channel, and defining delivery timing. In MVP, only email and push can actually be enabled; SMS is reserved for later phases once S‑03 SMS support is implemented.

nodes.title: Evaluate notification rules in real time

attrs.rationale: prd.md line 903 (REQ-030-003, verbatim).

nodes.title: Optional SMS for critical events, not in MVP

nodes.title: Template editor with variables and languages

attrs.rationale: prd.md line 924 (REQ-030-018, verbatim). Restating bullets merged here: Implementation Notes technology and threat mitigation (746, 789).

attrs.rationale: prd.md line 88 (Communication Structure, Out of Scope, heading line 82). One Rule per bullet under decision D52.

nodes.title: Super Admins invite admin team members by email

attrs.statement: System MUST allow Super Admins to invite new admin team members via email with role assignment
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-001. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Custom roles with per-module granular permissions

attrs.statement: System MUST support creation of custom roles with granular permission assignment per admin module (A-01 through A-10)
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-002. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Role-based access control on every admin endpoint and component

attrs.statement: System MUST enforce role-based access control on all admin API endpoints and UI components
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-003. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: System MUST provide predefined admin roles: Super Admin, Aftercare Specialist, Billing Staff, Support Staff
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-004. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System MUST provide centralized configuration for the four protected provider roles and for global custom provider roles created or cloned by Super Admins; custom roles require a non-Owner base type and cannot gain Owner-only capabilities
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-005. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: Provider role changes sync to Provider Platform within 5 seconds

attrs.statement: System MUST automatically sync provider role creation, cloning, and permission changes to Provider Platform (FR-009) within 5 seconds
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-006. Sync indicator and timing wording: see the sync and propagation rules; other propagation wordings conflict (migration report decision list). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: Owner role permissions cannot be reduced

attrs.statement: System MUST prevent modification of Owner role permissions that would remove full access to provider features
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-007.

nodes.title: Administrative actions logged in an immutable audit trail

attrs.statement: System MUST log all administrative actions (role changes, permission grants, user suspensions, access denials) in immutable audit trail
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-008. Business Rule 5 repeats this requirement (role changes, permission grants, user suspensions logged in the audit trail); merged here. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Last Super Admin cannot be suspended or deleted

attrs.statement: System MUST prevent suspension or deletion of the last Super Admin account (system protection)
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-009. Business Rule 4 repeats this (at least one active Super Admin must exist at all times, system protection against lockout); merged here. Tab 2 and User Story 6 scenario 2 disagree on whether a Super Admin can be suspended when another exists; see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Email notifications for invitations, role changes, resets and denials

attrs.statement: System MUST send email notifications for: new invitations, role changes, password resets, repeated access denials
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-010. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Role changes carry an Effective From date and time

attrs.statement: System MUST support role assignment changes with **Effective From** date/time tracking (stored and auditable)
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-011. Business Rule 8 repeats this (role assignments stored with an Effective From timestamp; enforcement respects that date/time on authorization checks); merged here. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain admin user accounts with: email, name, password hash, assigned role(s), role effective date/time, status (active/pending/suspended), creation date, last login timestamp
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-012. Key Entities, Entity 1 lists the same attributes plus the invitation token and MFA flag, and says one admin user has one assigned role; see the migration report decision list (single versus several roles). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain role definitions with: guard-scoped role name, description, assigned permissions (as permission matrix), system/custom status, and non-Owner base type for custom provider roles
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-013. Key Entities, Entity 2. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: System MUST maintain audit trail entries with: timestamp, user ID, action type, action details, IP address, outcome (success/failed/denied)
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-014. Privacy Rule 2 (IP addresses logged for security audit purposes, GDPR-compliant logging) merged here. Key Entities, Entity 3. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Audit trail retained for ten years

attrs.statement: System MUST retain audit trail for minimum 10 years per compliance requirements (Constitution Principle VI)
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-015. Privacy Rule 1 (audit trail entries immutable and retained for 10 years per Constitution Principle VI) merged here; Admin Editability lists the retention period as fixed in codebase. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System MUST be architected to support Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) integration as a planned Post-MVP requirement (per Constitution Principle II)
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-016. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System MUST use bcrypt (cost factor 12+) for password hashing
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-017. Technical requirement, kept because the PRD numbers it; Admin Editability lists the algorithm as fixed in codebase. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System MUST enforce password requirements: minimum 12 characters, 1 uppercase, 1 lowercase, 1 digit, 1 special character
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-018. Admin Editability lists the requirements as fixed in codebase. Governed by the existing FR-026 password policy setting (provider wording there; assumption recorded in the migration report). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System MUST sign JWT tokens with RS256 (asymmetric encryption) to prevent tampering
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-019. Technical requirement, kept because the PRD numbers it. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Authorization evaluated server-side on every call

attrs.statement: System MUST perform server-side authorization evaluation on each API call based on current role assignments and permission matrices; JWT tokens MUST NOT be the authoritative source of permissions
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-020. Business Rule 3 repeats this (latest role assignment and permission matrix evaluated on every API call; caching allowed only if invalidated within 5 seconds; enforcement reflects changes on the next API call after invalidation); merged here. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: Suspended accounts rejected from the next request

attrs.statement: System MUST invalidate active sessions (and/or reject access tokens) immediately upon account suspension; at minimum, all API calls MUST be rejected for suspended accounts starting with the next request
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-021. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Admin PII anonymised on deletion request

attrs.statement: System MUST anonymize admin user PII (email, name) on account deletion request, while preserving audit trail with anonymized identifier
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-022. The GDPR Compliance line in Data and Privacy Rules (email and name anonymised, audit trail preserved with anonymised identifiers) is merged here. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Email delivery through the Notification Service

attrs.statement: System MUST integrate with Notification Service (S-03) for email delivery (invitations, role changes, password resets)
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-023. Cross-FR citation: S-03 Notification Service. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Permission check API for admin modules

attrs.statement: System MUST provide permission check API for all admin modules to enforce access control
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-024. Technical requirement, kept because the PRD numbers it. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Permission matrix cached for fast checks

attrs.statement: System MUST cache permission matrix in memory for fast authorization checks (< 50ms per check)
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-025. Technical requirement, kept because the PRD numbers it. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System MUST invalidate permission cache within 5 seconds of role or permission changes
attrs.rationale: PRD Functional Requirements Summary, REQ-031-026. Business Rule 3 also states the 5-second invalidation limit. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: Super Admins access this module via "Settings > User Roles & Permissions" in the Admin Platform. The module is hidden from non-Super Admin users. The first Super Admin account is created during platform deployment/installation; later admin accounts are created through the invitation flow. Super Admins configure role permissions and invite admin team members; provider owners invite their team members (FR-009) but cannot configure role permissions.
attrs.rationale: Entry Points section; Data Dependencies (Admin User Accounts). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: Only Super Admins can access this module; regular admin users and providers cannot view or modify role permissions. The module is a Super Admin-only configuration tool and the single source of truth for role definitions and permission matrices across the platform.
attrs.rationale: Stated in the Executive Summary, Admin Platform scope, Entry Points and Screen 4 Access Control. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Provider Platform only enforces, never configures

attrs.statement: Provider Platform consumes and enforces the RBAC rules defined in the Admin Platform (FR-031) and has no configuration UI: provider users do not see or access role permission configuration, and Provider Platform reads permission matrices read-only and applies them when provider team members access features.
attrs.rationale: Provider Platform scope. Provider team member invitation and role assignment stay in FR-009; the permission definitions for those roles come from FR-031.

attrs.statement: Custom provider roles are global across provider organizations. Provider users may assign an available custom role to non-Owner staff in FR-009, but cannot create, clone, or edit role definitions.
attrs.rationale: Tab 3 business rule; Executive Summary and A5 outcome say the same. Overlaps FR-009 REQ-009-002 and REQ-009-149 (listed as possible duplicates in the migration report). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: MVP exclusions for admin notifications and sign-in

attrs.statement: No SMS admin notifications are available in MVP; SMS will only be enabled if and when S-03 adds SMS delivery in a later phase. Real-time permission updates via WebSocket and external identity provider integration (OAuth, SAML) are V2 enhancements and out of scope.
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure, Out of Scope. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Permission changes notified by email to affected admin users

attrs.statement: System sends an email notification to the affected admin users when the permissions of their role change.
attrs.rationale: Communication Structure lists permission-change email as in scope; REQ-031-010 names invitations, role changes, password resets and repeated access denials but not permission changes. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: The invitation form requires first name, last name, email address and an assigned role. First and last name are max 50 characters (letters, spaces, hyphens only); the email is converted to lowercase; phone number is optional (E.164 format); personal message is optional (max 500 characters, included in the invitation email). The form cannot be submitted until all required fields pass validation.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 data fields and business rules; Main Flow steps 6 to 7. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System validates the email format on blur or submit and shows the inline error "Please enter a valid email address"; after the Super Admin corrects it, the system re-validates and allows submission. Only valid email addresses are accepted.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B1; Screen 2 validation messages. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System checks the invitation email against all admin users (active, suspended, pending) and pending invitations; a duplicate is blocked with the error "This email is already part of the admin team" and the system suggests "View team member" or, if pending, "Resend invitation". The existing record is kept.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B2 and Screen 2. Screen 2 words the same error differently ("This email is already associated with an admin account. Please use a different email or check existing team members."); see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Only active admin roles can be assigned

attrs.statement: The role dropdown on the invitation form is populated from active admin roles only (archived roles excluded) and shows role name plus a brief description on hover; an expandable role permission summary is shown below it, and a role must be selected ("Please select a role for this team member."). Only active (non-archived) roles can be assigned to new or existing users.
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 business rules and notes; Data Dependencies (State: Active Roles). The PRD does not define how a role becomes archived. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: Invitation tokens expire after 7 days (168 hours). The expiry is configurable by Super Admin through A-09 settings within a range of 1 to 30 days.
attrs.rationale: Business Rule 6; Screen 2; Admin Editability (Editable and Configurable with Restrictions); Main Flow step 10. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: The invitation email carries the invitation link, Hairline Admin Platform branding and the role being offered, plus the personal message when provided. Before sending, the form can preview the email (invitee name, role, personal message, invitation link placeholder) and shows "Invitation will expire in 7 days on [date] at [time]". After sending, it shows "Invitation sent to [email]. They have 7 days to accept."
attrs.rationale: Main Flow steps 10 to 13; Screen 2 actions and notes. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: When an invitation is sent, System creates a pending invitation record with status "Invited", marks it "Accepted" when the account is created and shows it as "Expired" when the token has passed its expiry. The pending invitations list shows each invitation's status.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow steps 12 and 21; Alternative Flow A1. Status labels differ across the PRD ("Pending Send", "Delivery Failed", "Pending Activation", "Pending Invitation"); see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Invitation link validated before the setup form

attrs.statement: When the invitee opens the invitation link, System validates the token (not expired, not already used) before showing the Admin Account Setup screen pre-filled with email, first name and last name. An expired or invalid token redirects to an error page with a "Request New Invitation" option.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow steps 15 to 16; Screen 3 business rules. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Used invitation link shows a login message

attrs.statement: If the invitation link was already accepted, System shows "This invitation has already been used. Please log in with your existing credentials." and a login link, so no duplicate account is created.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B3. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Super Admin can resend an invitation

attrs.statement: A Super Admin can resend an invitation for a pending account, including an expired one: System generates a new token, sends a new email, and invalidates the old token. The invitee receives a fresh invitation with a new expiry. The pending invitations list shows a notification dot when invitations are about to expire (< 24 hours).
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A1; Admin Editability (re-send invitation emails for pending accounts); Screen 2 B2 suggestion; Screen 1 Tab 2 notes. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Invitation email delivery failure and retries

attrs.statement: If the invitation email fails to send, System logs the error and retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff; if all retries fail it marks the invitation "Pending Send" and warns the Super Admin "Invitation created but email failed. We'll retry automatically." A background job then retries every 10 minutes for 24 hours, and if still failing the system alerts the admin team.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B4 is followed. Edge Case 3 states a different outcome (3 attempts, then "Delivery Failed" with the Super Admin notified and a manual re-send); that reading is recorded as a decision item. External Dependencies: failed emails are queued for retry, failures are logged in the audit trail, and the admin team is notified if emails fail for 24+ hours. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: On Admin Account Setup, the email is pre-filled from the invitation and cannot be edited; first and last name are pre-filled but editable (2-50 characters; letters, spaces, hyphens only). The screen shows the assigned role ("You've been invited as [Role Name]"), the Super Admin's personal message when provided, and an invitation expiry countdown when less than 24 hours remain.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 data fields, business rules and notes. The invitation form (Screen 2) allows names up to 50 characters without a 2-character minimum. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: On Admin Account Setup, Confirm Password must match Password exactly ("Passwords do not match."). A password that does not meet the policy is rejected with "Password must be at least 12 characters with uppercase, lowercase, number, and special character from !@#$%^&(),.?\":{}|<>."
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 data fields and validation messages. The password policy itself is REQ-031-018 (defined in FR-026). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: The new admin user must accept the Terms of Service ("You must accept the Terms of Service to continue."); "Create Account" stays disabled until all required fields are valid and terms are accepted.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 data fields and business rules; Main Flow step 17 and 19. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Cancelling account setup invalidates the invitation

attrs.statement: Cancel on Admin Account Setup returns to the login page and invalidates the invitation token.
attrs.rationale: Screen 3 actions. The PRD does not say what status the invitation then holds or how the invitee gets a new one; see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: The phone number is optional for now (E.164 format) because MFA enrollment will be added in a future enhancement; Admin Account Setup shows an MFA enrollment section marked "Coming Soon" with the note "Multi-factor authentication will be required in future updates".
attrs.rationale: Screen 2 and Screen 3 business rules and notes. Related to REQ-031-016. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: When the new admin user clicks Create Account, System validates all inputs, creates the admin account with the role from the invitation, marks the invitation "Accepted", logs the account creation in the audit trail, sends a confirmation email to both the new admin user and the Super Admin who sent the invitation, shows "Account created successfully! Redirecting to login..." and redirects to the admin login page after 3 seconds. The new admin user can log in immediately.
attrs.rationale: Main Flow steps 17 to 25; Screen 3 Success Flow. User Story 1 expects the invitation email within 1 minute and the account status "Pending Activation" before acceptance. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Every admin user holds a role

attrs.statement: All admin users MUST have at least one role assigned (no "roleless" accounts).
attrs.rationale: Business Rule 1. Key Entities says one admin user has one assigned role, while REQ-031-012 says role(s); see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Super Admin role is locked to full access

attrs.statement: The Super Admin role MUST always have full system access and cannot be restricted: its permissions cannot be edited or removed, its checkboxes are disabled, and it stays locked in the matrix view.
attrs.rationale: Business Rule 2; Screen 1 Tab 1 rules; Screen 4 Admin Role Protection and Matrix Mode rules; Admin Editability (fixed in codebase). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: Edit Permissions, View Users and Clone Role are disabled for the Super Admin role.
attrs.rationale: Tab 1 data fields (Actions). Quoted as written; whether View Users should also be disabled is not stated. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Suspended admin users cannot log in

attrs.statement: Suspended admin users cannot log in but their accounts remain in the system (soft suspension, not deletion). Super Admins can suspend and reactivate admin accounts.
attrs.rationale: Business Rule 7; Tab 2 business rules and actions; Admin Editability. REQ-031-021 covers rejection of API calls. Tab 2 also says Super Admin accounts cannot be suspended by other users; see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Super Admins assign and change admin roles

attrs.statement: A Super Admin can assign or change the role of any admin user.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability (Editable by Super Admin); Alternative Flow A2. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: Role names of system-defined roles (admin and provider) MUST be immutable (not editable or renamable); the system admin roles are Super Admin, Aftercare Specialist, Billing Staff and Support Staff, and the protected provider roles are Owner, Manager, Clinical Staff and Billing Staff. Only custom roles can be renamed.
attrs.rationale: Business Rule 9; Screen 4 role name field (locked for system-defined roles); Admin Editability (fixed in codebase); Tab 1 and Tab 3 role name rules. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: System roles can be edited but not deleted

attrs.statement: System admin roles (Super Admin, Aftercare Specialist, Billing Staff, Support Staff) can be edited but not deleted. The four system-defined provider roles cannot be renamed or removed.
attrs.rationale: Tab 1 and Tab 3 business rules. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: Custom admin roles can be created, edited, and deleted (deleted only if no users are assigned). A role name is unique within the role's guard (max 50 characters) and a role description is required (max 500 characters). Clone Role creates a new custom admin role based on an existing role.
attrs.rationale: Tab 1 business rules and actions; Screen 4 data fields; Admin Editability. Custom-role deletion for provider roles is out of scope (separate rule). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: To create a custom admin role the Super Admin enters a role name and description and selects permissions in the permission matrix; System shows a permission summary with potential conflicts and warnings, validates a unique role name and at least one permission, saves the role, logs the creation in the audit trail, and lists the role in the Admin Roles tab and in the role dropdown for team member assignment.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A3. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: To create a custom provider role the Super Admin enters a unique role name and description, selects a non-Owner base type (Manager, Clinical Staff or Billing Staff) and at least one permission, reviews the effective access, sensitive-permission warnings and organization-wide impact, and confirms. System saves a global custom provider role, records the actor, base type and permission grants in the audit trail, and makes the role available for non-Owner staff assignment in FR-009.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A5; Screen 3 Tab 3 data fields and actions. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: A Super Admin can clone a system or custom provider role other than Owner: System shows the source role's base type and current permission snapshot, the Super Admin supplies a unique new name and description, and System copies the base type and eligible permissions into an editable draft, validates it with the same protected-action, dependency and sensitive-permission rules as creation, and after confirmation creates a separate global custom role with is_system_role = false. System logs the source role, copied permissions, actor and timestamp. Later edits to either role do not change the other, and cloning never creates a second Owner role or changes the source role.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A6; User Story 3 scenarios 6 and 7; Tab 3 actions (Owner has no Clone Role action). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: A custom provider role cannot use the Owner base type, replace the primary Owner, or receive Owner-only permissions; System rejects any attempt and keeps the single primary Owner invariant. Existing role-limited actions require both the applicable base type and the explicit permission grant: the base type defines eligibility, and selected permissions may narrow access but cannot bypass those protections. Cloning copies eligible grants without creating Owner-equivalent access.
attrs.rationale: Tab 3 business rules; Alternative Flow A5 step 4; Screen 4 Custom Provider Role Protection; User Story 3 scenario 7. Overlaps FR-009 REQ-009-149. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: Provider role deletion out of scope

attrs.statement: Deleting custom provider roles is outside the scope of this revision; custom provider roles can be created and cloned only by Super Admins.
attrs.rationale: Tab 3 business rules. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: Custom role base type fixed after creation

attrs.statement: A custom provider role's base type is required at creation (Manager, Clinical Staff or Billing Staff, never Owner) and cannot change after creation; Owner-only provider capabilities are fixed in the codebase.
attrs.rationale: Tab 3 data fields; Screen 4 Provider Base Type; Admin Editability (fixed in codebase). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: Configured matrix outranks the FR-009 default role descriptions

attrs.statement: Provider role descriptions in FR-009 are recommended defaults; the permission matrix configured in FR-031 is authoritative and may grant additional access (for example, Clinical Staff granted read-only financial reporting).
attrs.rationale: Provider Role Permission Rules (Provider Rule 1).

attrs.statement: Core permission categories (such as Patient Management, Provider Management and Billing) cannot be renamed or removed.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability (fixed in codebase). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Provider permission changes reach every holder of the role

attrs.statement: Provider role permission changes affect all provider team members with that role across all providers and are enforced on their next API call.
attrs.rationale: Tab 3 business rules; Alternative Flow A4 step 16 and outcome.

attrs.statement: The admin permissions Edit Settings, Manage Users and Manage Roles are write permissions reserved for Super Admin only.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 System Settings category (A-09); permission field is_super_admin_only. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Provider permissions limited to Owner or a base type

attrs.statement: Provider permission Manage Bank Details, Edit Settings and Remove Team Members are Owner only; Document Treatment is limited to Owner or Clinical Staff base type; Edit Team Member Roles (non-Owner) is limited to Owner or Manager base type.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 provider permission categories (PR-03, PR-05, PR-06, PR-01).

attrs.statement: The admin permission Issue Refunds is a write permission that requires approval.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 Billing & Financial category (A-05), access level "Write (requires approval)". The PRD does not say who approves; see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: Permission dependencies apply across all roles: selecting an Edit permission automatically selects the matching View permission (for example "Edit Patients" requires "View Patients") and the dependency is highlighted.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 Both Modes and Validation; Matrix Mode business rules; Alternative Flow A6 (dependency validation). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: A role cannot be saved with zero permissions

attrs.statement: System prevents saving a role with zero permissions: at least one permission is required.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 Both Modes; Single Role data fields (Permission Categories). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: Permissions are organised by module code (A-01, A-02 for admin; PR-01, PR-02 for provider) for traceability, and a Select All checkbox is available for each category.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 Both Modes. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: When a role contains permissions flagged "sensitive" in the permission definition (billing, user management, provider suspension, financial data), System shows a warning modal "This role grants access to sensitive features: [Billing & Financial Data, Process Payouts, View Transactions]. Confirm assignment?" together with the full permission summary; the Super Admin either confirms or cancels to select a different role.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B6; Screen 4 Validation. Key Entities Permission has no sensitive flag; ENT-permission.is_sensitive was added (orphan field). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: Impact confirmation before saving permission changes

attrs.statement: Before saving, System shows a confirmation "This will affect [X] users. Continue?"; for provider roles "This will affect [Y] team members across [Z] provider organizations. Continue?" and the headers warn "Changes will affect all provider organizations". When removing critical permissions it warns "This will remove access to [feature] for all Clinical Staff members" and shows the count of affected provider team members. In matrix mode the confirmation lists all affected roles and user counts.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A4 steps 8, 9; Screen 4 Validation and header; Tab 3 business rules and notes ("This change will affect [X] providers and [Y] team members"); Matrix Mode business rules. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: System shows a permission comparison before a change is confirmed: current versus new role permissions with the effective date/time on a role change, and additions and removals on a provider permission edit. After a provider role save it shows "Provider role permissions updated. Changes will take effect for all [Role] members on next page load."
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flows A2 step 7 and A4 steps 7 and 15. The "next page load" wording conflicts with next API call and 5 seconds elsewhere; see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: Reset to Default and Preview Impact

attrs.statement: In Single Role Mode, Reset to Default resets the role to the system-recommended permissions when they are available, and Preview Impact shows which users and providers will be affected by the changes. In matrix mode, Reset Role to Default resets the selected roles and asks for confirmation when unsaved changes exist.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 modal actions (both modes). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: The matrix view shows permissions as rows grouped by category/module and all roles of the same type (Admin or Provider, including custom roles) as columns, with checkboxes or access-level indicators. Super Admins can edit several roles at once and save all changes together; bulk actions are Select All on a column header, Select All on a row header, and Select Category; locked cells (Super Admin, Owner) show a lock icon and a disabled checkbox. The matrix can be filtered by category, searched by permission name, set to show only differences, sorted by role or permission, and exported to CSV or Excel.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 View Mode 2 (layout, features, modal actions, business rules). The example matrices are illustrative; see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: System tracks all permission changes against the saved state and shows a confirmation dialog ("Unsaved Changes" / "You have unsaved changes. Are you sure you want to discard them?" with Discard Changes, Save Changes and Cancel) when the user clicks Cancel, closes the modal with X or a backdrop click, switches between Single Role and Matrix view, or navigates away from the page. With no changes the modal closes immediately; the header shows an "Unsaved changes" indicator while changes exist.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 Unsaved Changes Protection. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: The Provider Roles tab shows "Last synced to Provider Platform: [timestamp]".
attrs.rationale: Tab 3 notes.

attrs.statement: Users Count (admin roles) and Total Users (provider roles) show, display-only, the number of admin users holding the role or the number of provider team members holding it across all providers. On the admin tab the count can be clicked to filter the Admin Users tab; View Users on a provider role links to FR-015 (Provider Management).
attrs.rationale: Tab 1 and Tab 3 data fields and actions. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: A permission change is logged in the audit trail with a before/after permission comparison: role name, permissions added and removed, affected provider count where applicable, timestamp and actor.
attrs.rationale: Screen 4 Both Modes; Alternative Flow A4 step 13; User Story 3 scenario 4. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

nodes.title: Role change for an existing admin user

attrs.statement: To change an admin user's role, the Super Admin opens Change Role, picks the new role and sets Effective From (default now); System shows the permission comparison and effective date/time, requires confirmation, validates that Effective From is not in the past, and updates the role assignment with the Effective From timestamp. System enforces the new role's permissions on the first API call at or after Effective From.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A2; Business Rule 8 and REQ-031-011. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System logs a role change in the audit trail with who changed it, the old role, the new role, effective_from and the timestamp.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A2 step 11. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: System emails the affected user about a role change, including the effective date/time, the old role, the new role and a summary of permission changes; User Story 5 expects it within 5 minutes. When a user then opens a feature they no longer have, access is denied with "Your permissions have changed. You no longer have access to this feature."
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow A2 step 12; User Story 5 scenarios 1 and 3. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Last Super Admin cannot change own role

attrs.statement: When only one Super Admin exists, that Super Admin cannot change their own role to a non-Super Admin role; the action is blocked with "You are the last Super Admin. Assign Super Admin role to another user before changing your role." A warning banner "Warning: Only one Super Admin account. Consider adding backup admin." is shown on the Admin Users tab while only one exists.
attrs.rationale: User Story 6 scenario 3; Tab 2 notes. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: If two Super Admins change the same user's role at once, database-level locking prevents concurrent updates: the second Super Admin receives "Role change failed - this user's role was just updated by another admin. Refresh and try again." and the audit trail logs both attempts with their outcomes (success, conflict).
attrs.rationale: Edge Case 2. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Active session survives a role change until the next API call

attrs.statement: When a role changes during an active session, the session stays valid until the next API call; that call checks the updated permissions and enforces the new role (the user may see a permission-denied result) and the session is not forcibly terminated.
attrs.rationale: Edge Case 1. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: On page load, System checks the user's permissions and hides menu items, buttons, tabs and sections for features the user cannot access, on both the Admin and Provider platforms. Only when hiding is not feasible (direct URL access, shared pages with partial access) does it deny access.
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B5 step 1, 2 and Note; Screen 4 UI Enforcement. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage. Provider-side application: Active stage.

attrs.statement: When access is denied System shows "Access Denied: You do not have permission to access this feature. Contact your administrator if you need access." and logs the denial in the audit trail (user, feature, timestamp, IP address).
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B5 steps 4 and 5; Screen 5 business rules (requested feature/endpoint). User Story 4 scenario 2 lists the same fields. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Repeated access denial alerts Super Admin

attrs.statement: System sends an alert to Super Admin if multiple failed access attempts are detected (potential security issue).
attrs.rationale: Alternative Flow B5 step 6; Communication Structure (system notifications for access denial attempts). The PRD does not define how many attempts or over what period; see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: All access to sensitive features (billing, patient medical data, provider financial data) MUST be logged with timestamp, user ID, action, IP address and outcome.
attrs.rationale: Data & Privacy Rules (Audit Rule). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: Password reset requests are logged in the audit trail with the requester's identity.
attrs.rationale: Data & Privacy Rules (Privacy Rule 3). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Super Admin sends a password reset

attrs.statement: Super Admins can send a password reset from the user detail page, which forces a password reset on the user's next login. A pending-activation account does not support password reset (no password set yet): the user must request a new invitation from a Super Admin, and the original invitation token is invalidated to prevent duplicate accounts.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 notes; Edge Case 4. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: The audit trail on the user detail page shows the last 100 actions by default with a Load More option; each row shows timestamp, action type (Login, Role Change, Permission Grant, Access Denied), details, IP address and outcome (Success, Failed, Denied). Sensitive actions (role changes, permission grants) are highlighted, and role change events offer a comparison of old and new role permissions. Login failures are logged with the reason (invalid password, account suspended, and so on).
attrs.rationale: Screen 5. Filtering by action type, date range and outcome is specified in FR-022 REQ-022-117 (cited, not restated). The PRD names six action types in Key Entities but four on the screen. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: The audit trail can be exported to CSV for compliance reporting, with all entries and the columns timestamp, user, action, details, IP address and outcome.
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 business rules; User Story 4 scenario 3. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Suspicious activity alerts on user detail

attrs.statement: The user detail page displays security alerts when suspicious activity is detected (multiple failed logins, unusual access patterns).
attrs.rationale: Screen 5 notes. No thresholds are defined. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Audit write failure blocks critical admin actions

attrs.statement: If an audit trail write fails, critical actions (role changes, suspensions) are buffered in memory and retried on database reconnection; if the buffer is full or the database is unavailable for an extended period, admin actions are temporarily blocked with "System maintenance in progress. Please try again shortly." and an alert goes to the infrastructure team immediately (audit trail failure is a critical security issue).
attrs.rationale: Edge Case 5; Implementation Notes (audit writes buffered, alert on audit write failure). Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

nodes.title: Admin user list paging, sorting and export

attrs.statement: The Admin Users list shows 25 users per page with a Load More option and can be sorted by Name (A-Z), Last Login (most recent first) and Role (alphabetical); the user list can be exported to CSV with all columns and the applied filters. Search and filters are specified in FR-022 REQ-022-115.
attrs.rationale: Tab 2 business rules and notes. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: The maximum failed login attempts before lockout, the session timeout duration and the number of concurrent sessions per admin user (default 3, range 1-5) are configurable in A-09 Authentication Settings.
attrs.rationale: Admin Editability (Configurable with Restrictions). The session timeout is linked to the existing SET-admin-inactivity-timeout (FR-026) on the assumption that they are the same setting. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.

attrs.statement: The admin login endpoint is rate-limited to prevent brute-force attacks (max 5 attempts per 15 minutes).
attrs.rationale: Implementation Notes, Security Considerations (threat mitigation). Promoted as a business rule because it states a numeric limit. How it relates to the configurable lockout threshold is unstated; see the migration report decision list. Stage placement for admin-side behaviour is provisional: the PRD names no stage and the model has no admin-configuration stage.
